When I first made the discovery of Poly Bridge my mind flashed to the Bridge Constructor which is a franchise by Clockstone Studio. They are very good games especially at the budget that they were made at. I enjoyed them immensely. I believe that they fit a relatively small niche quite nicely. As a result, I was skeptical that another title could prove to be a success. However, after over 1000 reviews on Steam with 89% of them being positive the game has been a critical success.
The title makes the game pretty self-explanatory. It takes polygon graphics and combines them with the mechanics of a bridge simulator to be Poly Bridge. The title is an engineer's dream. As a result, I wish that my uncle - who was one of the finest road engineers in Australia - was alive to play the game. Although he may have seen it as an extension of his work I believe that he would have been impressed. It seems like the type of game that even the professionals would be thoroughly impressed with.
The mechanics in the game are plentiful. This is in significant part owing to a wonderfully crafted event system. Things such as hydraulics can be designed for drawbridges, etc. One of the most enjoyable mechanics in the game is the jump system. You can essentially build a jump for your cars and bikes to jump from and as long as they clear the gap required it will be considered a success.
The mission system often relies on unrealistic bridge construction design that will both frustrate and inspire the imagination of players. They also demand players to meet multiple objectives. Thankfully, any mission can be skipped if it proves too difficult.
The presentation is clean and well designed. The UI is very simple and easy to use. The utilization of the grid system makes bridge architecture a breeze and the buttons are well placed.
One of the strengths of the design of the UI and the buttons are that every option has a hotkey. This makes things not only easier but faster as well.
There is also a well-implemented tutorial to provide the basic training that players will need. This is a great feature of the presentation. Finally, for those that need it there is also a well-presented manual that is accessible from within the game.
In comparison to Bridge Constructor, as much fun as I had with those particular games, this game offers significantly more. The gameplay provides greater depth and there is a lot more that the game enables the player to do. Though it remains a viable alternative I would advise newcomers to purchase this one.
From a Steamification perspective,  Poly Bridge is the Golden Gate Bridge. The game contains trading cards and Steam achievements. Secondly, the game delivers a competitive edge by incorporating Steam Leaderboards. Finally, and what satisfies me most of all is that the game incorporates the Steam workshop into the game. There is a level editor which enables players to create new levels and add them to the workshop for others to download.
Thankfully, the Steam Workshop incorporation has not fallen on deaf ears. Community members have already, as of writing, contributed well over one thousand new levels. They have further added two hundred autoplay pieces, 17 replicas of real life bridges including the famous George Washington Bridge and Golden Gate Bridge, 110 contraptions and 50 works of art. Hence, we can confirm that the community is an active one. The result is obvious. The community has given Poly Bridge a lifespan far beyond that of the over one hundred levels available in the base game.
Poly Bridge is not only a critical success but also a very pleasurable experience for all types of gamers. The game teaches you the mechanics of the game in a very thorough manner. This will enable casual gamers through to advanced gamers to get their groove on. The presentation is immaculate and well considered. If Dry Cactus are interested in further developing this game or creating a sequel I'd like to advise them to take up Tharodan's idea and create a management feature on top of the great puzzle game.

Princess Remedy in a World of Hurt is a short, fun bullet hell game for anyone looking for a quick introduction into the genre. text: Not the best game I've ever played, but I must admit that I got quite a bit of enjoyment out of it. For a free to play game, it's amazing. I've played horrible games that cost money, so I have some comparison at least. This style of game just isn't my style I guess.

A very simple game to get into, and you can take your time with it, if you like.  Hey, it's FREE, and it's worth trying, if you like cRPG elements, ship customisation, space combat & "exploration", shooters with bonus pickups, etc.
It's a fun little game in its own right, and the "space physics" (gravity vs thrust, Newtonian space vectored flight, etc) is enjoyably realised.  The art is simple, yet pleasant.  Game sounds are done well.  Controls are quite easy to master.
The "families" of ship designs are well presented, and make sense, and match the planetary artwork as well, which is a nice touch.  The "boss"-type ships are challenging enough that you'll definitely want to avoid them until you've done enough mining / resource gathering to afford yourself a bigger ship and better weaponry!!!
If you've played OLDer space-combat type games like STAR CONTROL, you'll find some similarities here, and it's very satisfying, actually.  If you've played EVEN OLDER games like ATARI's ASTEROIDS, the asteroid belts will definitely recall those old memories!  :P
If you ever played Origin Systems' AUTODUEL back in the day, and you were ever the "cautious" type, and learned to do the "slow-creep" approach which didn't trigger the radar-detected-but-just-off-screen enemy vehicles, then carefully "angled" your MG for a test shot, then adjusted your position until you got a hit and took them out that way,.. you'll find the cautious approach useful on some occasions here, too.  ;)
(No, that's not "cheating", that's "caution"; not everybody's play style is "going in gung-ho guns blazing"..)   ;p
Now, I'm not advocating a "hack" or "crack" or "exploit" here, but rather a curiosity-driven exploration of the game's "subystem" -- that is, withOUT any decompiling or any kind of source code manipulation...
If you're REALLY clever -- and since it's a Single Player game, not multiplayer / PvP, it hurts nobody (else) -- you CAN even "customise" your whole ship, including the ART... if you have the patience, and a calculator, and a simple pixel art-capable editor.  (MS Paint works just fine, esp if you Zoom In, and turn the Grid on!)
You COULD even "customise" the ship loadout, if you really wanted to...  I played it through the "long way", then I went digging.. just cuz I wanted to tweak how my ship looked.  :D
(The next time I put any TIME into this game, I /will/ create a YT-13xx-inspired ship, complete with turreted  laser cannon, and front-facing "concussion missile" launcher... just because it's possible!)  ((In fact, I'm betting others have ALREADY done this sort of thing!!  Yes? No?))
Invest $0 today.  Play it now.  It's not CS:GO, it's not FPS, it's not MOBA, it's not Overwatch, it's not Elite:Dangerous or Star Citizen... but it's fun for the smaller game it is, and more than worth the initial "investment".  ;)

Supposedly protected by 'Battle Eye' yet cheats and hacks still get through, not many but enough to fustrate you. There are specifc and seriously overpowered Pay2Win items, and you don't really stand a chance against those players. No down scale buffing for those that have all their skill trees maxed out, so you have players that move like lightning carry massive heavy weapons and massive damage reduction running around in new/amatuer games, the hare and the turtle parody. If you can get over the negatives, it is a pretty good game, and potential to go quite far. - Universal Gamer

When a visual novel is free, I usually go in with tempered expectations. At their best, they tend to be rough around the edges and at their worst, they can be downright terrible. Lucid9 bucks this trend and shows a high level of polish all around.
The overall story is great and keeps you on your toes throughout. It's definitely a story that draws you in and makes you want to see "just one more scene" in the wee hours of the night. The main cast of characters are all likable and have their own unique personalities. While there are some typical anime tropes thrown in, the characters show a remarkable amount of depth that makes the story that much more interesting. Both the music and the visuals are above average considering the price point.
This game is a good starter point for those that were interested in trying out a VN and don't know where to start. Even for those who have read a few VNs in the past, I consider this a must-read.
One word of warning to those interested: this game's story is still in development and leaves off on a massive cliffhanger. The developers are working on the next chapter of Lucid9 and will be releasing it, hopefully, in the near future. I am definitely one of the many who are earnestly awaiting the release of the next chapter!

This Review is written at the time of only the first arc being complete.
8.75 / 10
I honestly loved and adored this visual novel. I sat down to play and could not walk away until I had cleared it. The characters are all very unique and have interesting qualities and flaws. I found myself actually laughing with the characters at times and I was even panicking at times with them. I found myself deeply involved and pulled in to the store, and it is for that very reason that I do struggle to recommend this game. I reached the "To Be Continued" and I honestly feel like I died inside. I need more and I was absolutely at a loss to be left at such a cliff hanger. I love this story and want people to experience it, while at the same time, it is not complete, and I do not want people to be stuck in this mental break down that I am in. Decisions... decisions...

Lucid9 is truly an amazing game; one I would glady fork over $15 for.
STORY
While the game may appear cheerful and happy on the surface, it's quite dark and thought-provoking.
GAMEPLAY
No tricks thrown here. The game has a clean UI, lots of save slots, and branching endings. One improvement I would suggest is to add a typing-effect to the text where the characters individually appear instead of the whole sentance appearing at one go.
MUSIC/SFX
No complaints here. The game has a solid OST. My favorite track was "Meloncholy."
CHARACTERS
Very well developed characters. Each of them felt three-dimensional and didn't feel like plain old background characters. My only complaint is with the main character. I found his behavior and attitude throughout most of the game to be very annoying. Hopefully the sequel shows him mature in some departments.

Let me start by saying I'm not a huge indie game buff, but until my computer is fixed they're really all I can play on my laptop. That being said, Thomas Was Alone is a great game in almost every aspect. It's puzzle-platforming is engaging and fun, albeit not so challenging to where I ever got stuck. This, however, allowed the narrative to flow better and I personally feel that the subtexted messages behind the game were the real stars. The game doesn't offer much replayability (unless you like solving the same puzzles over and over), but there are so many different things to understand when you read into this game, and in my case it drives home the feeling that the story is what makes you attached to characters, and they don't necessarily need a face for the game to make you care about them. I was genuinely interested in the thoughts and opinions of a rectangle. All in all it took me around 4 hours to complete the game and I did it in one sitting, even obtaining every achievement on my first playthrough. It is a very fun game with an interesting plot.

Brilliant game because of its simplicity. Great storyline, music, and art (even if it is mostly rectangles). Doesn't take too long to complete either, and easy to pick back up, even after a long break.

Thomas Was Alone is an indie platformer with an array of different parallelogram protagonists and I freaking
it. Danny Wallace (Shaun from Assassin's Creed) narrates the story and does a wonderful job of making you care about a group of squares and rectangles. It's an adorable and brilliantly written story.
The gameplay is simple and the controls are easy to pick up on both keyboard and gamepad. Jumping can be a little unresponsive but that seems to be a limitation of the slower shapes rather than an actual break in the game. Also, if you're looking for a ball-bustingly challenging platformer, you won't find it here. The difficulty gradually progresses, of course, but it's forgiving with its checkpoints.
Simple as it is, it's still wonderful to look at. And I've been reliably informed I'm going to have my heart broken later. You should check it out, it's definately worth your time.

The most scary monster is the one, which our imagination is giving birth to. There's no book, no movie, no game possible, that can scare us. Our subconciousness is the only source of fear. We rely on our five senses. And when one of them is amputated, we are creating a momentary crutch of our imagination. In most cases we truly manage to find the route to the toilet with an amputated vision in the dark house at the night time. While we're dealing with the horror genre and a horror games in particular, the most gifted with a talent are those developers, who would imperceptibly turn our imagery crutch into a treacherous serpent. The venom of fear would poison our subconciousness absolutely, while we would not even notice that. We begin to expect that something horrible awaits us. And most frightening moments are those, when we just expect something terrible to happen, but in truth nothing is really happening. Rustles and unexpected noises, shadows and dark corners are just rustles and unexpected noises, shadows and dark corners. But we hear something horrible is sneaking around, we see that something terrible is hiding right here. The more obscurity, hints and glimpses we would be facing on our investigational "route to the toilet", the more frightened we would become. On our knees, scared to death by ourselves, we are crawling around in search of some clues of what's happening, of what's happened right before our appearence here. Intriguing mystery of the story is whipping us shamelessly. Sealed at the bilge we continue to row, thirsty to know about our final destination point. This is Slenderman. Frightening to death and simultaneously intriguing with a story, forcing you to move further and further. In contrast to the horror of what is happening environment is stunning, vast and placatory, open and gorgeous, enormously enhancing the sense of how defenceless, vulnerable, useless and lost we are here in the world of real wilderness. This is also Slenderman, a beauty on the outside with a monster inside.

So far, I feel pretty positive about this game!
Blueprint Tycoon is entirely about logistics - positioning buildings to make routes between them efficient, balancing production and consumption, and managing increasingly elaborate supply chains. Generally, it's the same kind of gameplay you get in games like Caesar 3 or Anno, but streamlined, and with little imaginative differences. For example, production buildings themselves have a little puzzle to them, reminiscent of SpaceChem but not nearly as difficult, which lets you optimise them if you want, although I've stuck with the defaults it gives you so far and not had trouble.
Early Access is no lie though - it's pretty rough around the edges. Stuff overflows the menus and windows sometimes, the notifications in the only scenario are way too frequent and distracting, and some of the UI is barely there at all. My biggest problem is a lack of clarity: that there's no way to see what a production building needs before placing it, you can't see what resources are on an island before buying it, when looking for a resource you can only check one island at a time, etc. I'm sure these will be ironed out as development continues but for now it is a bit frustrating to play.
It's hard not to recommend it at £2, and I look forward to seeing how it develops.

Remember Capitalism II where you had to buy the buildings and set up the supply chains and sell your stuff and the city would evolve around what you and your competitors did?

I think this is where this game wants to go.
You place down blue prints for workshops and other work buildings then set what they do internally then  set up the input and output. You need  provide housing and goods for workers to come to your island to work.
You start with an empty island to build on being mindful of resources and available fertility . As you work your way up the technology scale more types of resources are needed to produce to the next tier.

Poly Bridge is a lot like an engineering class. You start the game and some random old guy starts showing some super basic things. Like ok I get triangles, are my friends. Then he goes on to work through a few examples which seem pretty trivial. Then you move on to trying to do some of the book problems by yourself (ex: Alpine Meadow). It's a bit of a challenge, but after a few cups of coffee you figure it out. By that point you're thinking to yourself "I'm going to be a freaking God at this". And then comes the final exam where they ask you to create an elevator catapult which has to withstand the stress of an incoming boat. And just for ♥♥♥♥♥ and giggles, you also have to design a few Evil Knievel jumps which seem completely impractical and a public safety menace.
Basically, if you like physic based puzzles this game is for you. It may give you PTSD like my Fluid Dynamics class did to me back in the day, but in the end you get the satisfaction of having worked out the problem (or looked online for the answer, whichever I ain't judging). Oh and yes "triangles are your friend"...

The game features a 105-mission campaign mode with scenarios of good variety, thanks to the event system that triggers hydraulics (for drawbridges), ships, cars, and planes. Missions can also rely on “unrealistic” bridge structures like ramps and loops, further increasing diversity. Missions may also introduce checkpoints that require cars to pass through or turn around at specific locations. While scenarios are difficult, any mission can be freely skipped. A scenario editor and Steam workshop support are also included for even more content. The interface is done well, with the ability to copy-and-paste existing bridge designs and easily make arcs. Different materials (road, wood, steel, hydraulics, rope, cable) are used to construct each bridge, sometimes in limited supplies. Red static joints are used to fix the bridge to its surroundings, while split joints (formed by double-clicking) are used for draw bridges. The physics simulation is plausible. The elaborate event system, along with the ability to create multiple solutions, makes Poly Bridge stand out.

Normally I'd watch Let's Players play Visual Novels since they're not my cup of tea. But since this one was free and actually got my attention, I gave it a shot.
Lucid9 was an interesting experience that mixed the slice of life and mystery genre among others. It may look all cutesy and innocent sometimes, but trust me, it's far from it. It can switch from being light-heartedly comedic to darkly serious pretty quickly as you advance through the story.
You got your typical anime characters with their typical anime looks and typical anime personalities. But the thing that's not so typical, is the execution. Normally cliches would be a huge turnoff for some, but perhaps if executed correctly, it works so well that you actually grow attached to the characters.
Honestly, there's not a whole lot that I can say that hasn't been covered already.
You are given choices that may or may not affect the whole story, but don't throw everything away because of that.
Bad things can and will happen.
You will learn how quickly anything precious to you can be taken away at an instant.
You may like or dislike the characters, but you should perhaps sit down and listen; they all got a story to tell you.
And when you finish the story, you'll just want to say "Damn it all!"

But now, I am glad for the different game modes. And really... The only thing that has changed is that there are now badges, you can turn into a milk-carton mouse, and there are still clothes that make you look like a rejected Justin Bieber mouse. This part, I love- I mean, I get to be a mouse that has a mustache. I could have a fish hat. Seems like the future as we know it.
I recently started playing it again because I saw it finally made it on steam (congratulations, by the way), but I was very disappointed at how it had changed. Badges? Levels now? It's suddenly more of a MMO than a platformer.
The one thing I absolutely hate, and have read that many, MANY others do, is most (as not all of the community is like this- a very rare amount aren't) of the community. Most are homophobic, racist, or just plain out rude to new players. Tribes are difficult to get into. It's basically LoL for twelve and thirteen year olds- I saw so many people complaining about the "rushers" and how we need to work as a team. The new levels of shaman are difficult to master- there's like, what, 100 new things shamans can do? And trust me, it can get nasty if you don't have certain things people typically have as a shaman (i.e. the hearts, the spawning in people when they're dead, the apple, the wings, you get my point), and well... I'm disappointed. In 2011, the community was better, but now... really, the only peaceful gamemode is Delifante, because no one talks in it.
This community has driven me to write actually write a review- something I've never done before. Play it if you want, it's free. It's a great game on it's own- the concept is fun, and it's easy to get addicted to. But to really be accepted by the community, well- that's something I haven't figured out on my own. But hey, don't take my word for it. Play it for yourself, see how you like it. This is just my opinion, but, it's something many of the players have noticed. I'll continue playing the game on my own, but I do not recommend others joining in.
(Edit: I played this before it was on steam, hence why I said I've been playing it for four years. It's a game I go to every now and then, when I'm bored or really want entertainment from the stupid community. Still would not recommend.)

it. Danny Wallace (Shaun from Assassin's Creed) narrates the story and does a wonderful job of making you care about a group of squares and rectangles. It's an adorable and brilliantly written story.
The gameplay is simple and the controls are easy to pick up on both keyboard and gamepad. Jumping can be a little unresponsive but that seems to be a limitation of the slower shapes rather than an actual break in the game. Things that could be worked on:
There's several glitches with menus- not bad, just text clipping and accidentally clicking through them in places. That should be worked on.
I feel like I barely used blueprints. You click default blueprint, it works, and you move on. That's great, handy for making sure your production line works. However, the default blueprints should really be worse. I think it would be nice if you had  different blueprints for each tier, so when you upgraded, you spent a while designing more complicated, better blueprints. Otherwise, unless I'm really misunderstanding blueprints, there's little optimization that can be done from the default.
It would be cool if you could change where the input and output where on the blueprint. Maybe you'd have to redesign the blueprint around that. That would give more blueprints to design, at little programming effort, and much more freedom of construction at the logical cost of "Now things aren't lining up."
I think it'd be useful if there was a little more depth to carrything things around outside of factories. Upgrading and increasing workers is great and all, but maybe cars, trains? You could make it a lot more complicated, and add a lot more blueprints.
At a price of three dollars, it's worthwhile. The art, while simplistic, serves its purpose very well. Though there's a feeling of a lack of challenge. Maybe you have to deal with workers protesting for silly reasons, or other companies sabotaging?

This is a really good game, I love it, and so far this was the best Resident Evil game I played, the game is ok playing on single player, but it's a little more challenging and a lot more fun when playing it in multiplayer (be it with a friend or a complete stranger).
Its single but multi-perspective storyline is amazing, you get to play as all the early Resident Evil characters from the Racoon city incident and get to see how each of them contributes to the story of the game.
The character personalities were perfectly captured and have been brilliantly incorporated into the storyline.
I recommend this game to any player that has played at least Resident Evil 4, or they may be lost in where the characters originally hailed from.
The game does have its flaws though, the sniper doesn't have any way of being kept stable (holding breath for a few seconds) and crouching doesn't stabalize it that well either. Some enemies have glitches in them, where you would shoot them in the head and instead of exploding like its supposed to "regardless of weapon used" it just staggers back and readies itself for further combat.
Melee combat needs a lot of work, its rather difficult hitting a downed enemy, because the game sometimes doesn't register you standing on top/close to the enemy and then left clicking for the final finishing move doesn't appear viable.
The skill sets are quite tricky to manage as you can only have 3 skills active at a time and sometimes you desperately require a fourth skill for the mission ahead. Weapon upgrades would have been a nice addition but its loss is made up when you complete the game with every character by having all the infinite ammo skills availble for purchase in the skill setting menu.
Furthermore the game has a problem with ledges and cover, if you tried running to hurry up toward the next quest target and a jumpable ledge or cover point is close by, your character jumps the ledge or vaults the cover taking you back a few steps in the game. (Suggest changing the game's run button to any other rather than spacebar)
Overall I would give this game a 7/10 rating as the storyline is good and gameplay is somewhat easy to understand, the problems I've mentioned above cost it 2 points and the fact that some of the missions are so tediously long drops it another point.

First review on steam - That should say enough.
This game is a must have for anyone even thinking about stepping foot into the musical world. I am NOT musically inclined at all, but I love listening to music. I'm about 30 now. I played the drums as a kid in a drum core.. dont remember how to play.. and only memorized music from my brother, never knew what I was doing. I was forced to play the clarinet in high school marching band.. hated EVERY second of it. I skipped most of my band classes/practices and only showed up when it was a must... band just was not for me.. or so I thought. I always kind of felt a passion to make music, even spent a ton on a music producing program "Stagelight" and just can't figure it out. So to get on with it... my Birthday was this month, and my pops gave me an Amazon gift card for a couple hundo. Finally a music note slapped me in the face and BAM.. ordered an electric guitar. Never played a stringed instrument in my life.. no f**king clue what I was getting myself into.
I travel for a living so getting someone to help teach me just wont happen (lol) so I found myself picking up this game from Gamestop. I dont think I could be a happier man right now. Traveling around Cali, learning how to play guitar by myself.. actually making it sound good. My time shows 22.2 hours as of right now and I think 10 hours were AFK on accident. In those 12.2 hours though (5 days)... my fingers are getting trained by the session to not hurt, music notes are starting to come out, I feel very comfortable with a guitar now. I can't wait to rack up more hours on this game learning where my failing fingers need to be placed.
***This is said in below posts, but the one bad thing I wish was more in this game was learning how to read music and tabs. I've always heard to play guitar you really just need to learn tabs. This is something you will have to research on your own. There is tons of info on this online though.
I cant speak for the game as someone that already knew how to play guitar, but just starting out... this game is badass. If you have the opportunity, go balls out. You can pick up a great electric guitar online or in a pawn shop for less than $200.

Quite awful, but if the developers tried a little they could turn this into a decent game.
Pros:
-Killing creatures feels oddly satisfying, as if you're squishing a spider without all the mess involved

Ugh... this game.
First off, I think just about everyone should give it a try just to see what it's all about. That's the only reason it gets a thumbs-up.
That being said, I am not positive on this game or it's future.
First off, you should go watch this video:
This video is from the old Transformice, before the major graphics changes. I liked the old graphics system and wish they had stuck with it. The game has changed much since this video, but it gives you a really good idea of what it's all about.
I played Transformice way back when it was released in 2010 or whenever it was. It was wild, crazy, and full of ♥♥♥♥♥ gutter-scat. The trolling was actually pretty fun. Trolling is still potentially a part of the game today, but it's just not the same.
The idea behind Transformice is awesome. It's basically a chat room with a little mini-game system on top. Each mini-game is different, and timed. So, if you fail, you don't spend too much time being dead.
The mini-games are usually focused on a share of competition and cooperation. It's a big sociology experiment. Can you stick 50 people into a room and get them to solve a puzzle without killing themselves? Usually, no. Players almost inevitably end up killing both themselves and other mice around them through a combination of their action and inaction.
Individually, regular mice have almost no control over what happens in each game. Win and loss is collectively determined.
It's a good example of why crowds of people scare the hell out of me.
Unfrotunately for Transformice players, the game doesn't seem to be living up to it's potential. Development speed has been painfully slow. It's been something like five years since I last played it and the quantity of progress achieved over that time makes me sad. It's basically the same game with a few fixes, minor gameplay improvements, and pay-for cosmetics.
It's a very interesting concept. I had higher hopes for it, but I don't see the game really going anywhere from here. I don't think Steam will revive it either.

In a nutshell: I like this game, I like it a lot, and I don't like a lot of games.
In a nutshell 2.0: Why do I like this game?
It's interesting. You have so many different ways to play. You can play alone, you can play for the team, you can just help others and annoy Jason (my favourite). You can jump out and in from windows annoying jasons till they leave (free wins, I'm not complaining), you can go around looting houses and fixing things, you can hide away in a corner and make death people rage.. Fun things!
It's hard to get stuck on one playstyle, and I LOVE IT. The game incourages you to try new things with different houses, different stats, perks and Jasons.
You play as one of the two: You're either a camp counselor (most of the time), or actually the killer: Jason. To put it simply..
Are you a camp counselor? You must escape. You must survive. There is three ways to escape.
You can skip this part if you don't care about the details, but in a nutshell: there are options which make the game fun, since you can choose your way, your priorities and how you play.
> Fixing the car and escaping with it
- You need three items: The battery, the gas, and the keys.
- Fixing the car includes two reactiontime minigames, while putting the battery and the gas in.
- You need to drive away while Jason is following you, trying to stop you
+ Jason can only shift and teleport in front of you, which is hard in the road
+ Experienced drivers can go thru the woods, giving them more options
+ There is two types of cars: The yellow car (the two seater) and the blue car (the four seater) which randomly spawn in the map.
+ The most common type of escape
> Fixing the boat and escaping with it
- Similar to car, needs two items: The propeller and the gas
- Includes two minigames while putting the propeller and the gas in
- Most jasons have waterspeed
+ Water is a clear enviorement where you can easily go around without running into things
> Calling the cops
+ You need only one item: The fuse
+ Includes only one minigame while putting the gas in
- Jasons often trap the phone, making it harder to fix
- You need to wait 5 minutes for the cops to arrive
You can also just survive the 20 minutes until the game ends, where you don't die, but you still don't escape.
The game has many different characters with many different stats that affect how they're "supposed" to be played. Some camp counselors are fast runners, some are sneaky. Some can fix things easily, some are lucky and some can fight back. While some characters fit to some roles better than others, every character can be played as any role. Even if your character sucks at repairing things, you can roll a perk to balance that out.
Yes, the game also has perks. They're a fun way of customing your characters easily. You get perks pretty fast, I'd say you can roll one every two games in average. Even when you have a perk, you can get a version of it with betters %, making rolling perks worth it. Every characters can have 3 perks, and the perks are shared among all the counselors. That is ABSOLUTELY AMAZING. Why? It courages you to play different characters. You don't get stuck playing one role, one character, and even if you absolutely love Tiffany and her bootyshorts, you can play A.J anytime you want without losing anything. To give an example, the game "Dead by daylight" has a system which only courages you to main one character.
There is also different Jasons, but I don't really like playing Jason, so I can't tell that much of him. Jason has four abilities and his job is to kill everyone. He has some pretty epic kill animations. I like the potatosackhead jason. You wanna play jason? Sorry, can't help :c
Of course the game has some bad sides. The europe server is full of russians only speaking their language so voice chat is often useless. You can easily have a bad fps (I have around 30-40 with an old laptop) but it doesn't really make gameplay harder, apart from Jasons shift-ability being almost impossible to control. You can't change the controls (I'm still not used to where push to talk is, I think it's T for Talk..) and you can't really affect whether or not you are Jason, which is fair I guess, but I feel like I'm Jason more often as my friend.. which makes no sense with me prefering to spawn as counselor, him as jason. What.
Overall, I like the game. I bought it in 50% sale for me and my friend, and after playing it, I'd probably pay the full price again. And again. And.. still again. The game can be scary, the game can be goofy, and it can give you a ton of anxiety. But I love every piece of that anxiety. <3

I have tried to learn guitar a number of times before. My friends all told be "Just look at some YouTube Videos" or "just get some tabs and you're away". Realistically, you need 1 on 1 tuition to get started and for the price of a couple of lessons you can buy this game and a real tone cable. I am really glad I got this, it encourages me to pick up my guitar every day and practice. I am sure I will reach a wall in terms of how useful it is, but it got me over a lot of hurdles and gave me a lot of confidence. I still have a long way to go, but I feel like a have a path mapped out and I look forward to playing a little every day, which is always a good sign for musical instruments or games.
Based on discussions with a lot of my muso mates, I picked up a Yamaha Pacifica to use with this and it works really well. I have suffered no input lag with the real tone cable and I've really enjoyed how it lets me play the way I want to. I have learned a lot by playing the songs and then going into session mode and mucking about. I am not a huge fan of the arcade stuff, but it's easy to avoid.
If you've always wanted to learn to play then I think this is a really great place to start. Alternatively, if you have never really cared but have enjoyed playing games like Rock Band or Guitar Hero, this is the natural progression (a basic starter guitar like the Yamaha doesn't cost much more than the cheap plastic peripheral you need to buy for these games either, and it certainly feels a lot nicer to hold)

Pretty good game overall, although I enjoy it for different reasons than other RE games. Its definitely departed far from its survival horror roots, its much more of a 3rd person action game at this point with a robust combat system that is much more melee and dodge involved. There is a large selection of weapons that you just pick up as you go and ammo is never an issue it seems like, I actually ran into instances where I had to throw some away to make room in my inventory. Its an enjoyable action game though, as long as you have someone to play it with, I would not recommend doing most of the game yourself (although the partner AI is much better than it was in 5). There are several campaigns to go through and extra modes, like mercenaries, so you actually get quite a bit of content in this one. Theres also a bonus mercenaries mode for this pc release where you can play as Left 4 Dead 2 characters and special infected from that game show up, its a neat little addition that changes things up. I'll give it a solid recommendation, just don't expect it to be a survival horror game.

I enjoy the Resident Evil series, but with any of the older games I've always thought: "These controls are going to kill me." This was the first game in the series that I felt I had some real control over my character. And given the kind of crazy mutations you can fight in this series, it's good to have that much control. Dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge. I had a little trouble with some of the choices they made for the keyboard and mouse, mainly the in game inventory menu was a pain to navigate during heated moments. Otherwise, I feel Capcom did a good job on the PC port. Aiming is laser targeting still, but at least I have the accuracy of a mouse to help me aim. Turn up the camera and aiming FOV in the settings and you won't have any trouble playing on a monitor.
I know a lot of people hate this game because it's such a departure from the original games. But honestly, it's not too bad. There's a little bit in here for everyone. Leon has the classic zombie approach. Chris has an action approach. Jake has the constantly followed approach like with Nemesis or Mr X of the older titles. Ada has the puzzle approach. All of the campaigns can be played co-op or solo. Unlike other games where the AI partner is a bother or a frustrating escort mission, your AI partner stays out of trouble. They rarely die, they never run out of ammo, they never need your help. They're just an extra gun and stays out of your way. My only real complaint with the game is how the skills you can buy are almost a requirement. Until I got the Defense skill to reduce damage, I was constantly running out of health because the enemies otherwise do a ton of damage to you for simple bites.
I played through all 4 campaigns with just the primary characters. Some day I'll go back and play through with the other characters to enjoy the weapons and other paths I get to try with them. I picked this up 75% off and I definitely feel I got my money's worth. With all 4 campaigns and a little dabbling with the Mercenaries mode, I clocked in about 27 hours worth of content. With a future playthrough with the 2nd characters, I could see another 20 hours added in. I went into this game expecting a Resident Evil action game. I got what I expected and I'm okay with that. If you like the world and characters that Resident Evil created and just want a fun action game, this fits the bill. Don't go into this expecting a horror game and you'll probably enjoy yourself.

I just bought Nether today because my best friend recommended it to me. I was extremely skeptical because of the extremely negative reviews the game had gotten, but I still figured I would give it a chance since it was cheap. I have to say that while this game is definitely flawed, it is still absolutely awesome. There is not much of a storyline other than implication, but the game is just true exploration and survival. I almost feel like I am playing a dumbed down Fallout type of game, but there is still unique touches that make this game worth the purchase. First off, the game is very big on character/account development, and you get the typical experience points that make your account better. the difference with this game is that you don't respawn, but your account keeps the experience points. Every time you go into the world, you're at a fresh start as your character, and you just learn to get better. My absolute favorite part of the game is the Nether characters. What initially seemed like typical zombies are actually the scariest damn monsters I have seen in a video game. These nethers will teleport around you which makes a lot of intensity, and they do a lot of damage. The open world aspect of the game is quite amazing too, because there is so much to see and do, and scavenging for items is always a blast. I already have about 5 hours of gameplay in this game, and while I cannot call it perfect, I will definitely claim it to be massively underrated, and I recommend it to any fans of fps/open world games.

I wish this game had a price tag because it's worth at least $15. I would pay $50 in a heartbeat, if I knew the money would go to the staff.
I'd like to mention a few concerns first:
- Character art doesn't match the intensity of the story. Think Grisaia no Kajitsu, Katawa Shoujo, etc. The art definitely grew on me over the course of the story; I'm not trying to belittle it. I just hope no one has passed over this game because of that. Don't.
- Music was serviceable but not memorable.
- Lack of autonomy in certain areas - regardless of efficacy - was strange. A certain email exchange, for example, and the issue with Masato, and pretty much anything involving Natsuki. I assume they're setting up for a sequel, so hopefully some of these things will recieve focus in the future.
- Early, seemingly-minor decisions being important meant that viewing other paths required replaying almost the entire game. Text skipping with transitions off made this doable, but I still believe that texting the wrong person at the very beginning should count for less than the important choices you make toward the end. Anyone who cares enough about the game to view more than one path probably won't mind some extra text skipping, but the long turnaround time between the early choices and the ending choices does make finding the paths pretty frustrating. Also, personally I found it jarring during my first playthrough to see every CG and then get the Fruitless achievement.

And with the out of the way, here's some high-level Pros, because an exhaustive list of individual things I liked would hit the character limit:
- writing with depth and logic, and the kind of effortless quality that means it took blood, sweat, and tears to produce.
- thought-provoking riddles, puzzles, and questions. This game rewards critical thinking.
- fantastic characters and characterization.
- slick-looking UI and animations. I had assumed the game was made in Ren'Py, but according to their website they rolled their own. I wonder if some of the features can be ported into existing engine(s)? Thinking of the cell phone, HUD, and keyboard input in particular.

Sparkle ZERO is a bad game, and I can find very little good to say about it.
Sparkle ZERO is meant to be a simple game. You've probably played something like it before. You start as a small sparkle, and must go around eating things to grow. Visually, it looks alright. The soundtrack achieves what I'd imagine to be the game's goal. It is relaxing, but it doesn't stand out. I have no complaints starting out, except for the fact that the one button we need to know about, the one to move levels using the portal, is never told to you. I had to look that one up. If there are any other controls, I don't know about them.
Aside from that, the gameplay quickly becomes boring and repetitive. A few new "enemies" are added, though they never attack you and, at worst, are an annoyance. The most troublesome, I'd say, are the little gear-looking ones that swarm you and force you to move. Because of those, you may find it hard to use the aforementioned portals, as those require you to stay still. Regardless, it doesn't take long to grow dull and tedious.
Further on, more problems arise. My computer isn't great, but it should be able to handle a relatively small and simple game such as Sparkle ZERO. I've not yet finished the game, but the lag makes it nearly unplayable. I'm going to assume this is because of the game's insistence to load everything, including a few of the lower levels which you can see as you go about. The map gets to be frustrating because it gets to be rather helpful in the later levels but, because of how it looks, you will not be able to see it when moving upwards or to the left. Your sparkle will cover it up, having grown due to all of the food it has consumed. The enemies that were talked about before become much more detrimental to the progress of the game, the lag having made it nigh impossible to even get past the moving gears because you move too slow to see them coming and go to the next level before they're there. This game, supposed to be relaxing, can be so frustrating that you may have to quit for a bit in order to clear your head.
Overall, I would not say this game is worth it, or even that it is good. It is not good. Don't get this game. If you're looking for a relaxing game, this may start out as such, but will not last more than 10-20 minutes.

This is a great game for 2 reasons.
The first is the most game-related one, and is that it's a well-paced platform puzzle game with crisp, clear graphics that slowly teaches players the rules of the game and introduces new features.
It's nothing truly ground-breaking, but it's thoroughly playable and would have been a rewarding experience on its own.
The second is the narration. If you think you can't care about little featureless rectangles, well, you'd be surprised.
This game has an amazing story that touches on the titular loneliness, love, arrogance, having a purpose in life, friendship.
And all of it is told while you jump around with a handful of rectangles. The characters never speak, there are no cutscenes, just the narration, yet Thomas feels like a more rounded character (no pun intended) than most AAA-title protagonists.
Most definitely recommended heartily.

After reaching all 47 achievements, I guess its time for a review.  This game is the most awesome learning experience for a musical instrument I've ever encountered in any media.  I've tried learning guitar a few times in the past but it was boring and painful making it hard to stick with it.  This game isn't perfect but it gets so much right, you just want to keep coming back for more.  I hope this game has a very long life.
One of the achievements was bass only so I decided to get the Electro-Harmonix PitchFork pedal so I could switch between playing all 3 paths (lead, rhythm, bass) at the press of a button.  That was a great addition to my setup and opened up all the bass items which are a lot of fun too.  I'm playing with a basic starter guitar: Epiphone Special II.
Pros: The most motivating features for me were the achievements and the methods for grading your progress.  Each song has 5 ways of scoring your progress (Learn A Song percentage, 4 levels of Score Attack) that makes me want to ace them all.  Learn A Song supports a breadth-first progression through a song (gradually adding notes as you get better in each phrase) and Score Attack is an arcade-style depth first progression through a difficulty level (Easy, Medium, Hard, Master).  Master mode hides the notes and was scary at first but its a great motivator for weaning you off the sight-reading and encourages you to listen for cues instead.  Learn A Song also has Riff Repeater which allows you to mark a section and then slow it down and vary the difficulty level -- this is indispensible for getting those hard riffs down.  I also enjoyed working through the Lessons and Guitarcade.  Guitarcade is a collection of about a dozen games and they are an excellent way to get some technique practice in without feeling like you're doing something as boring as scales.  I'd really like to see more of these mini-games as they are much more fun than practice exercises.
Cons: Ubisoft sites really suck at consistency.  Achievements and unlocks are shown on the Ubisoft site, the Rocksmith site, and Steam.  Steam is rock solid but the others are woefully inconsistent and aggravating to use.  500 missions?  Really?  What an annoying achievement!  Guitarcade's Hurtling Hurdles seems much too sensitive and poorly balanced compared to the other games.  Session mode -- the mission system kept pushing this but I found it a dreadful bore since I'm not good enough to improvise anything interesting at this point..

Oh boy, Survarium. The game that so many compare to S.T.A.L.K.E.R. Don't even really know how I went from flight sims and dinosaur games to an MMO loosely wearing S.T.A.L.K.E.R.'s skin like a cheap prom dress, but hey, I'm open to new things.
Alright, witty intro achieved, lets get into my first and latest impressions, and what I believe the game needs in order to be great.
The Graphics: They're pretty great given the age of the game. Might want to consider upgrading your rig if you can't run say... World of Tanks on medium-high graphics. Not really much else to say. here
Gameplay: Oh lord, where do I even begin? Let's start off by saying that if your ping tends to go over 220ms, this game quickly becomes either a nightmare of death around every single corner with 0 hope to even defend yourself or you becoming a literal god on the battlefield, killing players left and right without so much as getting a scratch; I somehow had a kill:death ratio of 27:3 at level 5 with a PPSh because I was laggy that match. The core of the game is ok at best, I find player balancing is an issue, with new players getting matched up against level 20's with heavy body armor, AKM's with grips, sights, and silencers, etc. Your little PPSh-41 ain't gonna cut it in a match like that. As for the cheating people complain about, I personally haven't experienced any hackers/cheaters yet. Though anyone would be naive to assume there aren't any, even console has cheaters and hackers.
The anomalies are... interesting. Don't even bother going near them until you have high level gear. At level 7 with good armor (for my level) they still kill me in about 1.8 seconds. A few maps need balancing, namedly that one map with one team spawning in the hangar (the name escapes me). If you lose your foothold outside, you're done. The enemy team will continue to camp the only, narrow exit out of the building and get kill after kill at your spawn with little risk.
The devs can hymn and haw about the game not being pay-to-win, but premium gear allows players better chances when upgrading their weapon and further increase their stats (from what I've read in the upgrade menu) when upgrading compared to upgrading the same, non-premium weapon, as well as purchase better armor that; while players *can* get without having to buy into the game after grinding for weeks/months on end, is made available to them regardless of level. Not to mention XP boosts. That to me is an advantage towards people who purchased premium gear and therefore falls under pay-to-win.
PvE is, frankly, a joke. A player should never feel rushed out of something or forced to jump through hoops in order to access content. If you're lucky enough to get into a PvE match (I wasn't since no one plays it as you need to pay in order to close the other two player slots), you and your two teammates have 5 minutes to get through the level. In order to get a token to participate in PvE, you need to play 2 rounds of PvP.
--> joewillburn if you're reading this, I understand the need to test something, but you're going about it all wrong. The point of a test is to get as many people playing with the system as possible, not prohibit them as much as possible to 'reward' them with 5 minutes of coop that you need 2 friends in order to even try it, or have to pay to play by yourself or close one of the player slots after forcing them to play your PvP modes. That's not only low for a game dev, but low as a business strategy as well. Makes your team look like you're trying to bleed more money out of your playerbase rather than trying to provide the best experience possible. I can only hope you lower the value of the rewards gained for completing the PvE mission and make it unrestricted. I also pray your freeplay gamemode won't nearly be as restrictive as well. If it is, then I'd lose any hope for this game.<--
The Dev Team: I have absolutely zero experience with the team other than reading what joewillburn has replied with on reviews. So I'm not going to fuel what could very-well be either rumors of dev/moderator abuse or people lashing out for being punished for breaking rules (as a head admin for a game server, I know this happens a lot), to do so would be unprofessional.
Conclusion: all-in-all it's an OK game, but because of the development choices and business practices chosen by the team, I'm gonna have to lean more towards a negative recommendation. As with all my reviews they are subject to change. Should the game gain more balancing and the devs realize that forcing their playerbase to jump through hoops and climb pay walls to access the content they want isn't the way to go, I'll easily recommend this game.
Did I miss something? Have a different opinion? I wanna read about in the comments as long as you remain respectful, I won't tolerate anything less.
P.S.:  I don't know why so many people compare it to S.T.A.L.K.E.R., the only similarities are the fact that anomalies exist, and they aren't even the same ones from the series.

RE:6 is a pretty damn good game despite the hate some people give it. If one has to say it isn't a resident evil game anymore; I would say that the series really hasn't been "Resident Evil"  since code veronica or the first 3. It kind of got the hitman absolution treatment. Also going back to the city is wonderful since RE has been on this rural muddy/washed out colored binge for a couple games. They finally made a dark game again.. The addition of other game modes and mercenaries is also pretty awesome.
It remains linear though like 4-revelations which is my  small nitpick since I love to splore in games.
The only thing that bums me out is the (so-far) lack of weapon upgrade parts. The QTE's are actually pretty nice and short compared to other games where you can be asked to spam a key super fast for 30 sec.
I would easily give this an 7.5 to 8/10 if asked but to me I am fully satisfied and would really only want more re6. :P
More info:
I have been a fan of the RE series since playing/owning the first three at release on the ps1. I stepped away after code veronica and never cared to return since what I saw of four looked way too different from the RE games I knew and loved.
Only recently I have gotten into the later games 4,5, revelations and now six.
I would argue that they finally got rid of all the clunky mechanics that were only around because of the controllers and limits back then. While I love the old ones the best this one feels top notch gameplay wise out of the recent titles.
For instance the pause and shoot was from 1-veronica since you could not free aim and had to tap on the up down to shoot high or low. They kept it in 5 to be a throwback and somehow make it hard or something.
In Resident Evil 6 you can finally dodge and melee proper, though it will tire you and have a short cd. (non-spammy).
The gun play feels good and the sound effects are really nice. Being able to roll out of the way or land on your back to shoot from the floor is a great touch.  Graphically the game is beautiful and benefits greatly from Sweetfx.
In my opinion RE6 feels like what 4-revelations should have been controls wise. Those clung on to old mechanics to make you think they were staying true to the old play style. In 6 they shed all that, made the mechanics/controls more fluid/responsive and finally let it be a decent TPS instead of a slow clunky one.
This title takes you back to the city and the shambler type zombies come with that. You will find that sometimes it is better to run than it is to keep fighting. I wish we could have RE 1-veronica playstyle back but since that is gone, six is a good entry to the series.

I regret buying this.  My initial assessment was that it seemed pretty good.  The gameplay quickly degrades however.  It seems like this game is trying to emulate games from the COD or Gears of War franchises.  This could be ok if it didn't seem like actual gameplay was an afterthought.  It's as if they designed these set pieces or scenarios and then thought about how to shovel in gameplay afterward.  The first realization of this was in the gun shop scene: WE ARE IN A GUN SHOP WHERE IS THE AMMO?!   I'd assume the owner wouldn't be so stingy because it's a zombie apocalypse, but perhaps I assume too much.
Ok, then aftewards Leon and Helena are on a bus where a big fat zombie is holding up the front tires so they can't get away.  They have to survive other zombies' attacks, while trying to emtpy enough rounds into the big one's head through the front window.  Zombies come into the bus, they melee them, they shoot the bus lifter, rinse, repeat.  It takes too long to get enough ammo to do this.  I'm ok with making a game challenging via ammo crunch, but this just breaks the tension and gets BORING.  Not to mention our big uberbadass Leon has a fatigue gauge where he can't kick a zombie if it runs out.  When we're surrounded by very dumb NPCs (who don't shoot the ranged spitter zombies) and trying to survive by doing super badass moves (more on that later) it was very frustrating to have this happen.  Game to player: give zombies running bulldogs and sweet roundhouse kicks!  Player:  Ok sure!! Game:  Oh wait we gotta be like all realistic and like the other big blockbuster games, so nm hobble around.  Oh also player, you can't keep like a shovel or 2 by 4 these guys try to attack you with to attack them back.. cuz like, we wanna kinda also be like old arcade games.  We'll just keep the worst of both worlds to make it frustrating.  Player: Damn this kind of sucks I hope the next encounter doesn't suck like this.
So that gets done and it gets to the cathedral.  This was like in Wolverine Origin when they get to the island.  The game is cruising along, not good, not bad, and then the wheels just fall right off.  First off, this church has security statues with laser guided crossbows.  I'm assuming it's some kind of facility b/c of what happened next... so why would they have an odd, inneffective security system of this style, instead of some kind of modern sentry turret, or ya know, a locked door.  So that part is also really dumb.  Then there's the boss fight where a zombie will pick up Leon and tentacle♥♥♥♥♥♥his face if you press buttons wrong.  This was the last straw for me. Exactly what you expect from Resident Evil , I must say that I love this game. I love the addition of four stories instead of the usual one story with three difficulties. Like RE5, there is a co-op option, which I do take advantage of, since AI's are useless in every way aside from healing you. There is more to try to achieve with this game, unlike the others. You can track your unlocked files, achievements and game progress. Each campaign has an interlocked story, but they each have different overall skill usage. Leon's campaign is more defense, since you can stay safe in most all boss battles by just keeping distance of rolling on the ground. Jake's campaign is more melee, since there are parts of the game that you can only use Sherry's stun rod and Jake's hands to fight, they also don't give you a lot of ammo in this campaign. Chris is more firearm attacks, since they give you enemy after enemy that can't be taken down easily and they give you enough bullets that you'll have to shoot to make noise to keep room in your inventory. Ada's is mainly puzzles and quick thinking, since a few parts of the game are a race against time, and if you so much as run into a wall for too long of a second, you die. This was an excellent addition to the game, so it doesn't feel like the chapters and campaigns all run together. All over, this was a very great purchase. The game is a clean and easy install with no patches required for full function. The graphics are amazing. I have this on a Windows 7 x64 system .

If you've played a FPS in the last few years - then what Crysis 2 has to offer should not be mind blowing. Machine Guns, alien swarms, sniper rifles, grenades, headshots, shotguns, etc. Shoot a red barrel and it'll explode...yeah, it's all there. Personally, I would describe myself as quite "over" the FPS genre as a whole. However, that being said Crysis 2 manages to do all the typical FPS shooter mechanics extremely well... and throws in a couple of unique (although still not exactly not mind-blowing) little tweaks which is what makes this a really great game, and subsequently worth your time and money.
First off the single player campaign is both lengthy and well paced. The story (I have not played the original) is solid for the archetypical "Stop The Alien Scourge" type of deal. Coupled with really tight controls and a good swatch of weapons - it makes for a rewarding experience. The whole differentiator for the Crysis series is the suit that you are in control of. You can enter two modes which change the way you face each challenge. Being able to go "Stealth" (vis 'a vis the Predator effect) means that you can approach enemies unseen. Upgrades to your suit eventually allow you to perform more stealth kills and even walk through crowds of enemies unseen.
The second mode is an Armored mode. This basically allows you to go whole hog for a time and survive for a couple of hits longer then you normally would in a firefight. Doesn't make you invincible but it gives you a definite edge in both taking hits and dealing them out as well.
You can also run and jump which is considered "Power" mode, but honestly it's just another thing to drain your energy so that you can't zip around and be super armored at the same time.
Combining these two modes with a variety of customizable weapons, suit up-grades and tactical approaches provides a really interesting and robust way to tackle each encounter. You can literally approach the same scenario differently each time. I found the AI in this game both challenging and interesting at the same time. Enemies actually react to getting shot, hide well and as frustrating as a stealth kill that doesn't go unseen (although you think it should be) is - it's good that game doesn't mess around. There will be times when the AI just stands there or runs around sporadically but pound-4-pound it's more of an aberration than an annoying norm. And as someone who is generally kind of over this kind of game in particular that's high praise.
If you're a fan of the FPS genre then this should definitely be something you play. If you've never played a Crysis game and are burnt out on the FPS shooter genre (like myself) - this is still a great way to pass a Sunday afternoon. The graphics are indeed great, the gameplay is really tight and overall it's a really fun game.

Please Note: I was given a review copy by the game creator, for the purpose of this review. This game is also in early access and this review is current for the game version of April 3rd, 2016.
But now that the disclaimer is above and my bias gone, I must say that I really enjoy Blueprint Tycoon!
When it comes to gaming, I am a huge fan of games like RimWorld, Factorio, Spacechem, Big Pharma, and many others. It is beyond my own reasoning that games, like Spacechem, I love but yet play very little of due to the level of difficulty or increased effort in games with poor integration in teaching a player how to play. Spacechem was a game that screams in its influence into Blueprint Tycoon, from using the blueprints in individual processes at the many locations that produce and accept goods in BPT.
Now that being said, BPT does incredibly well where Spacechem failed. Spacechem was tough to learn due to the type of tutorial that it used to teach a player. BPT excels in teaching a player the basic concepts, then eases you in objective based learning on how to play the game. It took myself twenty minutes to learn and play, and further learning was then done on my own without help of the game. This is what makes BPT a lesser complexity then Spacechem, but the same level of depth in regards to what the player is doing.
With all that, BPT is complex, entertaining, and ever growing. In this early version, the game does have a long way to go but already has plenty of signs of incredible promise and a devoted set of creators. I look forward to playing this game more, touching on emotions and enjoyments from my days playing Theme Hospital, (attempting) Spacechem, and Big Pharma. Creating webs of production and supply, with that hint of business and logistical planning to create your island paradise. A game much like Anno, with a different level of depth and complexity, also has pushed influence into this game. Your island needs strong presence and attention, with the need to keep your people fed and trade strong.
There are a few downsides to the game however, in this early dev version (Obviously a work in progress) saves are buggy and can cause corrupted loading. Sometimes objectives are not good on explaining themselves, nor trigger completion when the player does the task. It is a little buggy, but never the end of the world or crashing out. A huge note here, this game is for early access and is obvious in its road to a complete game.
For the price paid present, it is an incredible display of what the creators want to go in their final complete game. I think it would make for a great game for those who loved games like Big Pharma, Spacechem, and Anno.

This in-depth review is as spoiler free as possible.
PLOT: 10/10
The first few minutes of the game make you feel like this will be your average visual novel where you choose between different girls and end up dating one of them at the end. Just your normal fluffy waifu simulator. But as the story progresses, the plot goes deeper than you would think.
Even though I was enjoying the light theme of the story at the beginning, I almost stopped playing because I thought that it would only go up to that. Boy, was I glad I didn't stop. This VN is intense, with you trying to make ends meet in your mind as to what is actually happening. If you're reading this, I advise you NOT TO STOP just a few hours in. You won't be able to grasp how well written this story is. But then again, if you're only looking for that fluffy otome style VN, maybe you should turn away.
CHARACTERS: 10/10
I loved the characters in this game. VNs usually only focus on the main girl you are aiming for. This game, on the other hand, lets you get to know all of the characters fairly, as long as you take the time to hang out with them of course. Each character has their own personalities and quirks that make them different from one another. Your relationships with them span from typical childhood friend to idiotic-but-lovable classmate, making your interactions with each of them different.
WRITING: 9/10
The writing was exquisite. Each character also had their own way of speaking and texting, with varying degrees in their vocabularies. I also loved the details put into this game. By the time you reach the climax, those minor details that you brushed off as insignificant all come flooding back. Those minor bits of foreshadowing all clump together to paint the entire picture. Just lovely.
ART: 8/10
It's your typical anime styled visual novel. It's clean, and the variety of expressions on the characters were good. The backgrounds were pretty as well. The small details like the characters zooming in when speaking worked really well.
MUSIC: 8/10
The background music really ties the feel of the scenes together. It's a great way to set the mood. Happy music for light-hearted scenes, and more solemn music for the more serious parts. Here's hoping that the future voice acting patch helps bring everything together as well.
OVERALL: 9/10
Very enjoyable, and easy to get hooked on. I can proudly say that my hours spent playing this VN have not gone to waste, especially for a free game. If you have even just a few hours of spare time, I highly recommend giving this game a shot.
P.S. I enjoyed the various easter eggs and shoutouts to different games. It made me feel that much closer to the characters.
Hands down one of the best free VNs on Steam. I'd have paid money for this. Play it, no question.

The storyline was way more than I ever expected for a free visual novel. Being around the same age as the characters in the story, it was relatable. I liked that the backstories of all the different characters were touched on. The plot was excellent. The happy moments were very light-hearted and serious moments were very intense. The music was beautiful. The only issues I had with it was that the body anatomies were a little off and the grammar could be improved on but it's free so I don't mind those.

A nice and very simple (and yet addictive in short sessions) card game. The first thing that will catch your eye it's the art style, which it's really cool and it feels taken out of old classic terror comic books. And yeah, the animation of each enemy it's just ok, with enough monster variety to keep things interesting for a while.
At first it may give you the impression that you just need to "smash" the different cards in order to win each battle, but then you realize that each enemy has a skill set of cards and different behaviours. You will start to loose soon enough and it's just at that moment that you're going to start thinking strategically your next move.
The game mechanics are really simple. You first start with 1on1 fights, then 1vs2 and so on till the last boss. As you keep defeating monsters you will unlock more cards and bonuses. I will say that the game it's fun for the most time and does a decent job at keeping you busy for a while.
The real problem is that there isn't enough enemy variations as I would like to see or maybe some more game mechanics (like for example a loot system with equipable items) to keep things fresh, specially after you realize what the game has to offer after a few minutes.
Also the lack of ingame music, the repetition of enemies and maybe the nature of the gameplay (just moving forward in the wasteland) will make things a bit dull.
It's a shame really because it could be so much more. But regardless of that it's an OK game with cool art style and enough content to have fun. And for the price, you get a really good deal.
I recommend it for any card game enthusiast and for people who are looking to play something while listening to some podcats/youtube videos etc. Just don't expect nothing to hardcore.

This game tells you no lies. You watch at the trailers, and that's exactly what it looks like.
Pros:
+ Cards are interesting and there is a decent variety of them
Cons:
- Monsters are hideous (in the bad way)
- There is not story
- There is no objective
- It gets really repetitive, very fast
- This theme has nothing Lovecraftian in it; not even close
Verdict:
A boring yet challenging fighting card game, maybe for niche players.
Long description:
You are a biker and you cross a desert full of monsters. The trip is made of three steps, each of them composed of three encounters, and ending with a boss. During the first step, each encounter has one monster, in the second, it has two, and in the third, yep, it has three.
You fight monsters in two ways: in each passing second your character shoots at the monster and deals one damage (but so does the monster to you) and you play cards (and the monster does as well). Cards have a cooldown before the effect applies once you played it. Better cards have longer cooldown, needless to say. Each card is withdrawn once played. You get back all your cards by the end of the encounter (so you have to play more and more long-term strategies as you go further in your trip).  You `build' your deck by choosing between two cards at several points of the trip: at the very beginning, after the first encounter of each step, or something like that. It means your deck is made of a very limited number of cards.
And that's all. No objectives, no story, no lore, nothing. Pure card game with some weird and ugly theme. It may please some for its challenge and is strategic-thinking.
Nowhere close to a roguelike. You'll be far beyond boredom before you unlock half the cards.

This game packs a lot of style and fun in a simple package, It is relentlessly focussed on play dropping you right in the game and back to the start when the game ends, which is minor but a refreshing change from the typical game with lots of menus and cut scenes wasting your time. This one has confidence in what it is delivering and delivers it proudly.
Each game you collect a small deck of cards each of which can be used once against a monster or set of monsters. In this way each run feels fresh because you are building a new deck which will be played differently than other decks.
The game play itself involves timing the cards for maximum effect, and managing your meager card resources to survive the cirrent pod of monsters. The game moves fast but I wouldn't say it is reflex oriented, it is more about fast tactical decision making.
I wouldn't expect more than a few hours of play from this, but those hours are probably good and well priced if you like this description. I currently have 6, and will probably play a few more.

At first, I didn't like this game. The controls seemed overly-complicated, the story lines were somewhat lackluster, and the general atmosphere for some of the campaigns just didn't feel like 'Resident Evil' at all. So much has been done to this series since Resident Evil 5, and it kind of feels like Capcom wanted to shift directions for the series, so they ended up trying to make it like a Hollywood Blockbuster movie instead of a survival horror game as it should be, but that's an argument for another time.
The campaigns are separated into Leon (Helena), Chris (Piers), Jake (Shelly) and Ada Wong's own campaign. There's a Mercenaries Mode which is 'okay' to an extent, but my own personal gripe is that there's not enough characters outside of the story mode (unlike RE5) and no one has their own signature music, which I miss. Other than that, I enjoy it, and the whole unlockable perks thing they have going on is kind of a hit and miss. It really depends on your taste; me personally, I enjoyed just buying and upgrading my weapons ala Resident Evil 4, though they could have done it in a way where you didn't need a merchant, but you could buy upgrades in between rounds and such, but again that's all just my preference. Instead, the game has you pick up these little Chess pieces that give you points, and you spend the points on corresponding perks, i.e. faster reloading, steady aim, critical shots, more stamina, etc. The builds you make with your perks carry with you through the story mode and mercenaries mode, respectively.
As for the stories themselves, I'd say Leon's is the most accurate to the franchise, Jake's is somewhere in the middle if not entirely on it's own, and Chris' campaign I dislike the most, simply because it's this non-stop action fiesta and there's not enough 'horror' where their should be, but again that's just a personal gripe. As for the other DLC modes, I haven't played them yet because sadly there is a lack of an online community, so that's kind of a pitfall.
Other than that, some of the level's set pieces are amazing, the graphics are on par with the current generation, and everything else is as it stands. I'm not too fond of the inventory system, but it lets you switch everything up on the fly without having to keep pausing the game everything you need to switch weapons. All in all it's still a fun game, it just lacks focus.

I would say this game is only for devout fans of the game series. But I find myself questioning if I'm a fan after this. First, there are WAY too many quick time events. It's too the point where I just want to enjoy a cutscene and open a door without having to work for it. It doesn't add to difficulty or fun, it's just irritating. If you don't have good reflexes, you'll die A LOT.
The additions to combat are interesting but feels a bit clunky. I like that you can melee and counter enemy attacks. They've also added the ability to dodge. It can be a bit overwhelming when you first start playing. The controls aren't very intuitive. I like where they're going with combat but they may need to simplify it a little. With all the new additions, it ends up feeling messy. That being said, the combat is probably my favorite part of the game. Which is why I enjoy Mercenaries mode the most.
The difficulty is iffy. There are times when I might write it off as lack of familiarity or I'm just clumsy. But there are also times when it just feels like the game expects you to die over and over just to learn the game. Dying over and over to learn the mechanics gets frustrating. The game ends up feeling unrewarding and rather than progessing you feel like you're regressing.
The story makes as much sense as the films. But I do enjoy the characters. If there was one redeeming feature, it would be the graphics. The detail in character faces and models are really lovely.
So tl;dr: This game isn't that great. But if you enjoy shooting and kicking a zombie in the face, this game might be passable.
