Short: A splendedly free game without any in-game purchases or gimmicks. Great way to spend an hour or so, however, expect to run into a lack of content (as of 2/10/2015).
Long:
Pros:
+ Free without gimmicks
+ No paying for anything
+ No ads/etc.
+ Decent combat system
+ Physics are decent (one exception, see below)
+ Semi-realistic propulsion (no air resistance in space)
+ VERY responsive development team
Cons:
- Severely lacking in content/Underdeveloped (in current state)
- No music
- Limited number of ships
- Limited number of weapons
- Grindy
- Lacking direction
- Unclear controls (other than those revealed in the tutorial
- Tutorial does not cover all controls
- Cannot re-bind controls to a custom setup
- Movement can be inconvenient
- No way of slowing in space, except for turning ship around and firing rockets
- If your ship tips over on a planet, you may get stuck/have to ram a tower or hill in order to re-orient yourself
- Limited areas to visit
- Items get stuck on rocks/debris, and since they pull towards you, it can cause you to gain momentum in an inconvenient direction. Coupled with no way of slowing/stopping and sometimes an almost impossible ability to turn the ship, this can be a near game-killer on a semi-frequent basis.
- Warp gates can get stuck on eachother, making for a very amusing, albeit twitchy and very deadly mess.
- Enemy AI can be weak at times.
- You can simply hide at a nearby station, abuse them to blow up said station, then reap the profits of both sides' deaths.
- Additionally, some of the larger enemy ships get stuck within a planet's sphere of influence, and seem unable/unwilling to escape.
- "Orbiting" enemies, particularly machinegunners, seem to be an almost non-existant threat.
Things that could be developed/Suggestions/Ideas for development:
= Music
= More areas to visit
= More ships and weapons
= Possibly carrier-class ships for when the amount of allies gets out of hand
= Could lead to larger battles
= Bug fixes
= Introduction of a ship-based cargo hold system (larger ships have larger capacity)
= Game Direction/Objectives
= Trading/Merchanting
= Completable missions yielding profit/items
= Possible multiplayer functionality
= Air resistance on planets
= Orbiting
= UI improvements/Graphical updates
= Anti-aliasing
Even though I've put more improvements and cons than I did pros, I still think this game has a solid base to it, it's just lacking in content as of this moment. The content it currently has is quality, we just need more of it. I'm hopeful that the developers continue to add content to this, and if so, I wouldn't mind throwing a few dollars its way.
MY RATING: 6/10
(If anything, try it for yourself, see what you like/dislike, it is free, after all)

Slenderman games originally came to be when Mark Hadley(AKA Parsec Productions)released Slender the Eight Pages as a freeware game for Mac and PC on June 2012,and later some maps dubbed"Slenderman's Shadow"were released also as a freeware game by Marc Steene,starting on August 2012,and the games were immensely popular,prompting Mark Hadley to create a sequel,and of course Marc Steene to release more maps,which eventually got made into a full game,and the sequel by Mark Hadley(and another developer named Blue Isle Studios)was officially announced around when Slenderman's Shadow got started,August/September 2012.
The game was first released as a"beta"on February 2013 for Mac/PC,which was just the 2nd Level"The Eight Pages",and was officially fully released as a full game on March 28,2013
It also got a rerelease on Steam for Windows on October 28,2013,and later Mac and Xbox 360 versions on September 2014(which is also when the DLC stuff was added).
I originally bought this game when it originally came out for Mac/PC on March 28,2013.
Then I got the Steam version for Windows in May 2014,and still was barely scared at the game,but still really liked the game :).
Then I bought the Mac version just recently,and after playing the 2 new DLC levels,I can say that this game is AMAZING ^_^
The basic plot(possible spoilers btw): There are these 2 sisters named Kate and Lauren(and 2 other people named CR and Charlie Matheson Jr.,that you'll find out about in detail in the 2 DLC levels). Kate keeps having visions of the Slenderman and decides to move out of her house and sell it,which prompts Lauren to investigate and visit since she's a real estate agent. Her car gets stopped by a tree,so Lauren goes to Kate's  house on foot, finding her stuff/furniture all over the place,and drawings of Slenderman all over Kate's room and on the walls. She hears Kate scream and goes out to investigate.  She finds the 8 pages in the forest and is almost kidnapped by the Slenderman and tries to escape,but blacks out.  She then flips on the 6 generators in the Kullman mine,occasionally getting caught by Kate(as a proxy,basically a servant being mind-controlled by Slenderman)and escapes on an elevator.  She finds a tape and sees that Kate was turned into a proxy by Slenderman,she then finds another tape(first DLC level),where CR is investigating what happened to Charlie and gets killed by Charlie,who was also turned into a proxy.  She then goes to the radio tower as Kate's notes instructed her,but the forest bursts into flames and Slenderman occasionally appears,trying to block Lauren's path.  She evades the Slenderman and goes into the radio tower,where she finds a tape,plays it in the camera that's sitting next to CR's charred corpse,which reveals how CR was killed(won't spoil how tho). Charlie(as a proxy)runs up to Lauren and she blacks out.  She ends up in a destroyed-looking home,and after looking at a couple of notes(from Kate I'm not sure myself),hears crying.  She goes to investigate the crying,which turns out to be Kate,and Kate kills her,and the camera shows  Lauren being dragged offscreen(by I believe Slenderman,again not sure myself),and the camera shuts off,ending the game.
In addition to the main story there's also 2 DLC levels(including the one I mentioned with CR,the other one I won't spoil),and a level called"Genesis",which is a remake of the game that started it all,The Eight Pages :)
The music is amazing,tho the game mainly relies on ambiance and atmosphere.
The characters are pretty good,and the voice acting as well(tho there's not a whole lot of actual voice acting).
The levels are really cool,tho they can get kind of repetitive with the gameplay at times I'll admit(even as a huge fan of this game)
The atmosphere is probably the best part of the game(in my opinion at least), and I can guarantee that at least 1 time you'll get scared,brave with horror games or not(in fact,I actually cried once because I was so scared xD).
Overall,this game is an amazing horror game that I recommend to everyone,and I applaud Mark Hadley and Parsec Productions for making this game,and Marc Steene for making Slenderman's Shadow,seriously I do :)

tl;dr: Game's literally pointless with god awful hit detection. For details, continue reading:
'Pointless' is a game all about clicking dots, and no, it's just not that simple. Not because it isn't simple, but because it isn't programmed to be simple. Not because it's clearly intentional. But because the programming just basically sucks. And you know it does when the first thing you're greeted with is a mock Gameboy screen meant to bring up nostalgia of a two-bit variety, only making the game look cheap and completely unoriginal, not to mention make you want to pull out that old brick of a portable handheld instead of play this. On top of that you have a repetitive score and random sound effects that mirror that system's capabilities, yet quickly grate on your nerves the more time you spend listening to them. Honestly, some of the cheap knock-off handheld companies back in the day had higher standards, though the Nintendo today may be willing to slap it up on their DS/3DS e-store.
Of course the huge problem about this title becomes immediately apparent with the first click of the mouse once the actual "game" starts, and that is the hit detection is pure garbage. No, I wasn't just sitting here clicking tiny dots on a filthy laptop screen, though I admit it did happen more times than I'd like to admit to, but I found myself clicking upwards of twenty times rapid fire to get one single dot, only to watch it vanish and be forced to move on to the next in hopes of actually gaining that one point. In just ten seconds I conceded it'd just be easier to sit around waiting for the L power-up to show so I could have a little fun with it without the use of an auto-clicker hotkey script running in the background in a feeble attempt to rack up achievements to my Steam account.
On top of that, 'Pointless' has no penalty system in place, so sitting around in no way hinders your progress. You're best bet is to just click and use one of five weapons, only three of which seem to have any real use. Pulse places three pulsating obstacles on the screen at points of your choice and, if done right, will spread the dots and rack up thousands in one go. Bomb is nice if you have a number of clustered dots on screen as well. But then you have laser, which is the most enjoyable, allowing you to hold the left mouse button down and automatically click. This one is best done by making small circular motions to rack up a decent amount of dots. These three work very well together if done right as well, but long (black rectangle that crushes dots) has minimal benefit. There's also chain, but I genuinely have no idea what it does, if anything at all.
There are a few options, but they are as basic, and disappointing, as the title itself. There's music and sound effect volume controls, as well as an option to change the background "color palette", but only after you destroy so many dots to unlock the other two distinctly bland colors of peach and tomato red. Yes, that's all the cosmetic changes the development team has allowed. God forbid you get a third color scheme to unlock or new "game girl" handheld border because  us clicking pointlesly at pointless dots wouldn't possibly know what to do with that much power at our disposal other than watch the credits and add our pointless total to a pointless global score to show the world how collectively pathetic we as Steam users are in this day and age.
Thankfully for achievement hunters, these are simple to rack up with some help. If you have an auto-clicker program or a script that runs in Hotkey, something I wound up abusing by the six thousand dot mark and realized how little I could be bothered to try to click the many fleas infesting the digital handheld device that wouldn't die even when I properly clicked on them in the first damn place. You can scoff at the idea but, trust me, it's almost necessary to do this since you have to have the game the active window at all times in order to get any weapons or new dots to appear on the screen.
'Flea Extermination Simulator 2016' is, well, a thing that exists. Is it a game? Not necessarily. Remember the old 'Game & Watch' style of handheld games? Well just picture a bunch of fleas somehow got into one of those, and it's up to you to exterminate them all before they take over your house. This is 'Pointless', both in title and execution. The only goal this title serves is to add another cheap and quick one hundred percent complete title to the list of Steam games with achievements. Sadly, without caving and using an auto-clicker, you'll find it quite a tendious, fairly broken experience that will leave you questioning where you went wrong in life that you're playing something worse than the recently released failure that is 'Bonsai'. Hopefully the developer becomes kind enough to throw some bonus colors or backgrounds into the mix, maybe an actual game or mini-game to breathe life into this waste of a dollar but, until then, 'Pointless' is an absolutely "pointless" experience for anyone who's game completion percentage score and achievement count doesn't mean the world to them.

Biohazard 6 is a difficult game to class. On the one hand, it does so many things right, and on the other, some things horribly wrong.
The story is split into 4 campaigns, each with their own gameplay and style; Leon S. Kennedy and Helena Harper team up to take on a traditional zombie outbreak, Chris Redfield and Piers Nevans have an all-out war on terror, Jake Muller and Sherry Burkin battle near-invincible bosses, and Ada Wong solves both gameplay and plot puzzles. Leon and Helena's campaign is the best, with a great atmosphere and fun gameplay involving traditional zombies, with Ada's campaign 2nd for it's plot and puzzle elements. Jake and Sherry have the most unique gameplay, due to Jake's Melee ability complimenting Sherry's ranged ability, with QTEs holding it back from being the better. Chris and Piers share the worst of the four, with their campaign being about as cliche and boring as your average military bromance story. They do crossover, both in terms of style, gameplay and story, and they do all contribute to an overarching story, which is convoluted but interesting enough that it held my attention from beginning to end.
Gameplay is were the game really shines and shows it's unique identity. Movement and combat is a smooth, fast and fluid ride for the most part, broken up by the bane of my existence: Quick Time Events. With gameplay as good as it is, I'm simply lost to find any reason why they thought filling their game with these boring, tiresome interactive cinematics. The excellent combat mechanics, which include dodges, rolls, cover and some character specific moves, are more than enough to carry the game. The other stuff on offer, however, is not. Some driving sequences from Chris and Jake's campaigns are more painful than fun, Ada's helicoper level is mostly boring point and click, and some other odd choices make some sections of the campaign more trouble than it's worth. Multiplayer also handles an odd mix; while the basic combat mechanics are great in modes such as Mercenaries, Mercenaries No Hope, Versus and the other modes that handle normal characters play well, others, such as Agent Hunt, which puts you in the role of a zombie in the campaign, controls awful and feels sluggish. Also, don't bother with the gamepad. It works, but barely, and the keyboard has hotkeys which will make your gameplay experience so much better.
The music and audio is all around high quality, with excellent voice acting, great music and fantastic audio cues enhance the gameplay and the story to awesome hieghts. It played exceptionally well on my 5.1 Surround Sound system and was a thrill to blast the sound to it's maximum levels.
Graphics are all around great. The HUD is small and keeps out of the way for the most part, but the itmes menu could have been handled better. The textures are decent aside from some low-res environmental textures, and the lighting is beautiful. Animations, Capcoms strongest point, I think, is fantastic, though some feel like they're too exagerated and overlong. The art design holds up well and is overall a great-looking game.

This is the most important maneuver: How to "Wall Jump" (WJ). This is possible due to friction on upright surfaces, and that you can jump in mid-air if you walk off a platform - When you jump into a wall and keep running into it, the game thinks you're on the ground again (due to friction), so you may then jump off the wall and return again to repeat (It is easier to practice and get your timing right on "Chocolate" walls (higher friction). Basically if you want to scale a wall on your right, you run right, jump into wall so that you are FALLING as you hit it (after highest arc of jump). If you hold RIGHT as you fall into the wall, your mouse should start to slowly slide down the wall while "running" into it. At this point, you STOP holding the RIGHT key down so that you are now free falling, tap LEFT to get away from the wall, you may NOW JUMP to get additional height and return to the wall. (remember to wait until you are past your jump arc to return to the wall and repeat the process). The Wall Jump will NOT work if your mouse is not FALLING as he/she contacts the wall. The game really opens up when you learn how to do this. It just takes practice.

So lets get down to the review:
If you have played games like Dungeon Siege, Divine Divinity or even Arcanum you will probably like this game.
I see lots of people comparing this to these games with action combat and almost non existant stories (like Titan Quest) and that is not what this game is.
Pros:
- The parts that are voiced are well done, nothing cringe worthy
- The story is great, with a fully fleshed out game world with history and culture.
- This game has a nice take on the classic fantasy races, for example in the game elves are no longer    pretty and have resorted to wearing specially designed masks to make themselves look presentable again.
- The companions you meet have their own unique personalities and none of them feel like carbon copies of another.
- While the game has grim moments there is lots of comedy as well, like a goblin who wishes for food and gets killed by evil chickens or a book all about how everyone but elves are dirty peasents (written by an elf btw)
- The game has this nice feature where item that are just laying on the ground can be picked up and moved around as you like (same feature as in Divine Divinity), rare to find in these top down rpg games.
- Crafting is a big part of this game and it is fun to play around with. It covers everything from cooking to blacksmithing and there is no shortage of things you can make.
Cons:
- Combat is simple, not really a bad thing but it def has the feel of a more D&D type combat system where the damage you do is based purely on level and a dice roll. The game has a classless system where you only gain Skills (weapons skills like double strike on melee weapons or you get spells like fireball from staves) from equiptment you wear so if you plan to play a mage then you really have to pay attention to what gear you use.
- Some mobs will ambush you from out of nowhere, and its not like they pop out of a near by bush or something no, i've been attacked by thieves that seemingly fell out of the sky.
- Some skills have odd animations, as a bit of a connection to my last point, the skill "Leap" does exatly what it sounds like, you leap at a target but the animations are odd. instead of having your character leap at something, they leap into the sky, vanish off screen, and then you see them fall down at the location. I'm not sure why a regular old leap animation was so hard that they had to turn leap into teleport but okay.
Overall this game is fun to play with only a few issues, but for such a small price its a great deal.
9/10
EDIT:
Someone pointed out that a feature that i thought wasnt in the game (saved recipe list) was actualy just something that i missed in game, the review has been edited to reflect this.

A game like "Rocksmith" is truly a difficult thing to review. There are so many different concepts to music and to how people want to evolve their talent that no one opinion will do justice to this game. It functions and provides a great distraction to rote training, but it honestly is not the best tool around.
For starters, "Rocksmith 2014" does not have the best tutorial around. I guess with the rise of the YouTube era, everything is taught to you by a quick video. You are then tasked with plucking strings and holding frets without any knowledge of why. The game neglects to go farther into music theory, as well. I suppose a quick lesson on tremolos will do, but that honestly isn't going to elevate your skills farther.
The next musical sin comes from the explanation of notes. If you play bass, you might as well skip this game. The game constantly badgers you to check the note book, but then only includes that option for lead guitar. Even then, there is no further elaboration on how to properly place your fingers or what the root of each note stems from.
There are no detailed looks into intervals, timing, self-tuning or note patterns. You simply are told to place your finger on fret 5 and play it on the first string. It would be nice to know that is an A Note, but I suppose that little detail is irrelevant.
If your only interest in music is learning how to play a very select assortment of songs, then sure; "Rocksmith 2014" will allow you to play those songs. You will more than likely sound sloppy and have no form, but man can you rock out to 'You Really Got Me'.
In the end, I haven't spent eons with the game. The only reason I got it was because I figured it would be a good supplement to my regular music lessons. It hasn't failed in getting me more interested in playing, but it definitely has held me back from growing as a musician.
I suppose this game is really only intended for those who are bored with their instrument or want to augment their playing into a really standard and unskilled manner. You will be better served calling up a good teacher and getting yourself taught the basics of music theory.
5/10

I purchased RS2014 just wanting it to be a "game" like Rockband or Guitar Hero.
I didn't have a real interest in learning to actually play the guitar (I've tried numerous times in the past and given up), all I wanted from this was something I could casually play, but with a bit more challenge/reward than the "plastic guitar" games.
It started off exactly how I was expecting - just playing a single note every now and then, but as you improve and play the notes its' giving you well the game will adjust and add more into the mix. Before too long you'll be given chords, double-stops, legato techniques, and plenty of other new bits to play.
The way the difficulty works is good, it won't give you something to play that's way over your head (too often), but keeps you improving at a good rate.
In the few weeks I've been playing, I've progressed a lot further with my skills than I have in all my previous attemps to learn guitar without Rocksmith. I'm interested in learning to play again, and this makes it a great way to do it.
Pros:
* Very cost-effective way to learn (if you already own a guitar).
* Being able to have your skills quantified (Mastery percentage, song accuracy, scores etc) and improving is great motivation to see your progress and keep playing.
* Makes practicing fun!
Cons:
* Music choice is decent, but could do with a lot more songs. New songs are released every week though.
* There's no option to see the music to play in Tab format.
Overall, I highly recommend it, it's a lot of fun and you learn something while you play.

Rocksmith 2014 is not only for beginners who want to learn how to play, but also for fairly experienced players who wants to improve their skills or simply take advantage of the many tools in-game.
There are several modes:
''Learn A Song'' which allows you to play along to one of the songs that are included in the game or can be bought as a DLC. It might be remind you a bit about games like Guitar Hero. The difficulty adapts after how good you are, and get harder and harder as you learn more and more.
''Session Mode'' gives you a virtual band to play with! You can customize and choose your scales, tempo, groove, atmosphere (club, studio, arena) and what instruments that is in your band. Or you can load up a stock one, like ''Electric Blues'' or ''Psychedelic Rock'' all after what music you intend to play.
There are also a whole catalouge of lessons that learns you everything from playing chords and the basic scales (and even how to hold your guitar, lel), through harmonics, hammer-on's and pull-off's, to the master classes.
Also there are arcade style mini-games that let's you train on your tecnhicques. Temple of Bends, Scale Warrior and Harmonic Heist are some examples.
Along with that you get some very useful tools. The tuner which allows you not only to standardize your tuning, but also change into different tunings based on the song you are playing. So it might be smart to plan ahead so you aren't stuck too long in the tuner. Also you get ''Tone Editor'' which allows you to change your effects, pedals and amps. Coolest product placement ever with Eden, Orange and Marshall. Every song that you play also have an ''authentic tone'' that loads up when you start the song. If for example the solo and the riff has different tones in a song it changes automatically. You can also load up these in Tone Editor so you can play with it in Session Mode.
The included songs ranges from hits like ''My Generation'' and ''We Are The Champions'' to songs from underated indie bands that no one has ever heard of. Try to play every song, you might find something you like. If you have the original Rocksmith you can import them with updated tabs or you can buy it if you didn't own it previosly.
Looking at the large amount of DLC, it's easy to think of this as another ''DLC: The Game'' but it isn't. New songs are released to this game constantly, but the artists need to be paid. So you have to pay for the license.
If a song you like hasn't been released however, you can download custom songs for free using some modding tools. They might be faulty however since they are made by sparetime modders.

There are some things to remember though: This is not Rock Band or Guitar Hero. You might and should have fun while playing this game, but remember it's an educational game. This means that you can't expect to learn the songs by playing it over and over again. You have to go deeper and use the ''Riff Repeater''. Riff Repeater allows you to slow down certain sections of a song and play it at any speed you want, again and again until you get it.
Also this is a TOOL not some kind of potion that magically transforms you into Jimmy Page. The challenge to take the skills you learn in the game into the real world might be tough. Sometimes you will find yourself cutting shortcuts just to hit the notes, which makes things even worse (espescially when soloing). If you really want to learn, you are gonna have to use other means too.
In short: It is a great game if you want to learn the basics of guitar/bass, improve your skills or just have some fun. Use it with caution and don't rely solely on it if you want to learn guitar properly. Great songs, good tabs and useful tools. It's worth buying for every aspiring or aspired guitar player out there.

In keeping to writing reviews for these small indie teams, critiquing and applauding, this game is a at least decent in terms of being a game.
(No spoilers)
In short, this is extremely casual game. Puzzles and platforming never become that challenging, and the controls are not oriented for that of an action platformer.
This game exists for it's story, charm, and visual quality.
Again the gameplay is quite weak because of this. The hand drawn art style definately went before everything else, and the season changing is neat, but it still seems quite minor.
As far as the story goes, it presses you forward quite nicely after a bit too linear opening. The 100% ending gives closure (100% [not in steam achivements] isn't that hard to aquire), but I can tell you without spoiling, the final cutscene is underwhelming.
As far as extra critique that I wish this game had? More moves from this adorable fox. Look up and crouch animations could have been there just to give the character you play in even more charm.
Why do I say this even though it isn't that significant? In games like Shovel Knight. pressing down meant nothing to play, but you could dance to the music. (Fancy!, Exquisite!, Absolutely) Useless(!), but charming.
Same for a game like Hollow Knight, that had up and down looking animations, that were not always necessary for progression either, but gave you detail in how the character looked (you could even fake bow with it)
A minor gripe, but that's just cause I wanted to see that cute fox do more.
Otherwise, I'd say this game is best worth it on an under $10 sale, as it's gameplay comes out more to be a 2D walking simulator with a glorious art panel behind you.
-If you do get the game, the name is significant to understanding the ending. Just write that down and think about it later.

Storyline: Annoyed emo chic Violett gets drags off to the "country" by her upset/angry parents to her uncle's (?) delapitated house, and ends up having a very bizarre adventure like Alice, Corinne or Dorothy (Wizard of Oz, movie; the OZ books are even more bizarre).  The environments are a tad creepy in nonsensical, illogical and flat out bizarre type of way, much like Wonderland, Oz or where ever Corinne took place, are.
And to all those "there is no story line" complainers out there please explain to me how Alice in Wonderland made any sense at all, ever, in either book or any of the countless movies (and movie remakes).  Violett's entire storyline occurs during the preliminary movie, and has absolutely no bearing on the adventure.

Puzzles: Unique and with some very obscure clues at times, plus the gamer really has to look at the details in the background to realize what to do in some cases.  Good for that out of the box thinking and improving those observational skills.  The logic for the puzzles is there, a tad obsure at times, I admit, but if the gamer takes the TIME to LOOK FOR and TALK TO all the characters, the characters will explain pictorially what to do.
Worst puzzle: Chimneys.  Not difficult to figure out just timed.  I knew what to do but was highly frustrated by the fact it took so long to do it.  Only time I needed a hint, and the hint I needed was that the puzzle was timed.  (It would have been easier to do with a reset button too.)
A side note to the puzzles and overall concept: this game makes far more sense and is far easy to play then Limbo.
While playing watch Violett.  If she makes a negative Uh-huh sound while vertically moving her hands the gamer is on the wrong track.  If she puts her hand under her chin in a thoughtful pose then the gamer is on right track.  She is the best clue giver in the game.
For most gamers I would say the biggest drawback is actually taking the TIME to look around and examine the objects while thinking about what to do and where to do it.  Half way through the game the gamer starts accumulating an inventory which needs to be used in another environment.
Collecting orbs:  In my first playthrough I collected 80+, 90+, 90+ of the orbs.  Unfortunately some of the green orbs are so well hidden the gamer needs a guide to find them. (They are invisible basically and the gamer needs to know exactly where they are.)   Collecting orbs takes TIME, a keen eye, and just a bit of intuitive thinking.  They are needed for the end game, so the more the gamer has, the better off the gamer is. (I highly recommend Dspecht's orb hunting guide.)
Overall: Wonderful game with whimsical if not fantiful music.  Simple yet highly detailed environments. Logic puzzles based solely on the "thinking" of illogical characters (In other words, what to do would make sense to them, not us.)  Admittedly the end game surprised me, I definitely was not expecting it.
Biggest drawback: TIME.  From all the reviews and comments I have read after I played this game time seems to be the biggest complaint.  This game took me a couple of hours to play through the first time, in a very leisurely and casual manner.  I enjoyed it immensely, looking at the detailed environments, chuckling over the diary pages, and simply shaking my head in amusement at the overall bizarreness.  This is not the type of game to speedrun or meant to do as fast as possible.  This game is meant to casually stroll through, while doing things like solve puzzles.  If an action packed speedrun type of game is what you want then this is not the game for you.

Well. The game's art is great and so is the music. For some reason the main character is the worst looking thing in the game.
Violett moves to a spooky house in the country with her parents. She seems unhappy about it. In her room she discovers a magical amulet in a mouse hole. This takes her to a magical world of fairies and bugs. Think Coraline with a lighter tone and more colours.
This game is incredibly frustrating in many ways. Some times it's hard to know where you can walk because of the layout of the map. Some times this is solved by the creators by putting an arrow in the landscape, so I guess they realised their error and fixed it an easy way. The clickables sometimes changes the mousecursor to an 'available action' hand, some times not.
As a completelist I haven't been this frustrated about collectibles since as long as I can remember. The orbs are sometimes easy to spot, some times can only been seen from certain angles, sometimes actually invisible. Some of the hidden places are the same way; some easy to spot some you will only see in a guide.
If you miss the orbs or diary page in the first room, there is no way to go back and you'll have to start a new game if you want the completist achievements. There is also a bug that happens sometimes where Violett will get stuck for no reason and you'll have to exit and load game to fix it. As far as I can tell from internet searches and guides I collected all the diary pages needed for the achievement, yet I did not get it.
The voiceacting. I don't mind gibberish-language games, but some of the voices in this game is just plain annoying. And ofcourse the one you'll hear the most, Violett, is the most annoying of them all. The sound Violett makes when she tells you she can't do whatever action you tried to make her do, is one of the most annoying sounds ever and you feel severely punished for not clicking everything perfectly. Add to this that it's impossible to turn off the sound effects; you can only turn it down to level 1/10. All of this makes it 100% necessary to use a guide at all times, which always makes the game less fun.
Violett collects pages from her uncle's diary throughout the game, but nothing is told by the game of who the uncle is, how and why he was in the same world Violett discovered.

Imagine the concept of the orrignal Asteroids game fleshed out into a more hardcore production. Taking the simple thrust-turn-shoot mechanic and adding RPG and roguelike elements, and painting an aesthetic reminiscent of titles like FTL or AI War: Fleet Command (an overall product that reminds me of the Realspace 2). This could easily sell in the five dollar or greater range, though it could have just as easily been a f2p browser-based flash game in an earlier era. In an even earlier era, I'm pretty sure something similar went for about 25 cents per play, back when Atari made cabinets. ;)
Bottom line: give it a go. It's Asteroids with the depth and look of FTL, and there's even a bit of Moonlander mixed in when you land on a planet! And it's free!

What a wonderful game! For a game made in a game jam (and then edited some afterwards) this is much more in-depth than I expected! True, the game only takes around an hour to complete, but then there's higher difficulties and the multitude of endings possible (each one is only different by like two sentences but still) and plenty of secrets. I only beat it once at time of writing but I plan on trying the other diffitulties and getting 100%, as I only got 97%.
The gameplay is fairly simple: heal people. You talk to them to see their problem(s) and shoot at them with your healing abilities in a 2D shooter/bullet hell format. It's kind of weird due to the fact that you always shoot in the direction you're facing and you can't change it, but I think it adds to the difficulty. Speaking of, this game's difficulty is strangely up-and-down. For the first couple of areas I was breezing through them like a Nascar driver on speed, but suddenly I had to try some healing again and again because of how much the difficulty increased suddenly. Then a bit later, it became easy street again. Then hard. It's all over the place, but it's not bad since losses don't have penalties.
The story is simple: heal everybody, and heal the Prince! There's not much of a story, but there doesn't need to be. Older games that this is mimicing generally had about this much of a story, if not less, so it emulates it well. All of the characters you speak to have some really funny lines, and I feel like the comedy was done well. Whenever I think "that joke has kind of become slightly overused," the joke ends and another begins. That's key to good comedy.
Get the game. It's 10mb, free, and fun. The only reason you wouldn't get this game is if you prefer story to gameplay or graphics to fun. I honestly feel like playing it for free was a steal, and I should have paid for this. Could there at least be a little DLC that's like $1 that includes artwork and a thank you note? I'd pay for it, even if it was more than $1. Would you believe me if I said it was made by (I think) 4 people! Crazy!

Prepare to immerse yourself in this nostalgic game featuring great music and gameplay. You explore a world in a 3rd person view similar to Breath Of Fire and Pokemon; in which you open chests to obtain objects that help advance your stats, and initiating "battles" passively when you encounter a sick NPC.The battles are known as "Healing mode" in which you face off enemy viruses by controlling the direction your princess moves and also where she fires "medicine". Another "weapon" you have are flasks which can be thrown as grenades. Enemies range from non-moving patches to gliding ghosts that shoot stuff at you, trying to cut down your health bar. I do reccomend this game for anyone who's interested in short RPG games, or just something to pass the time. It's free too, which is a huge bonus! However, if you were to make a sequel to this game, I would suggest that you make it a paid game. I would've paid for this game if I had watched a few gameplay videos first. Ember is an amazing RPG.
Well ok maybe I haven't played enough to say that, but I have played enough to know that it is worth 2 if not 3 times the asking price it launched at. So at this price I can only heartily recommend it.
Bottomline is that I am having a lot of fun, more than I had with my first two hours in DAO for instance.
Below are just some things I thought were really nifty.
Looting feels more substantial in this game then any other (CRPG) I've played. In others you'll packrat all the useless junk you find along the way like rusty nails, broken plates other paraphanlia that makes you feel more like a hobo filling his stolen shopping cart than a grand adventurer. Then you'll go to the shops and sell everything (or as much as you can carry) and realize you'll have to choose between loading up on potions and getting that really cool +1 type item you want.
Whereas in this I picked up everything in the starting dungeon (99 iventory with no weight) almost filling my inventory and once I sold it all I had over 2000 gold and could really gear up my chars AND load up on potions.
Granted perhaps it doesn't make sense that there are precious stones littered about all over the place, but once you get to the shop you don't care anymore.
Also at the same time it actually makese sense that practically every corpse would be fully lootable unlike in some other games where you get a shield from that one, nothing from the next and a sword from the other guy.
This world is absolutely filled with stuff you can packrat.
(Some) Wolves roam realistically. The 3rd area you get to is the forest (many areas have seamless transition by the way) and here I came across a pack of wolves that were roaming and chasing down deer, not as a cutscene, as ingame behaviour. Then the pack continued patrolling after killing the last deer heading straight for my party.
The visual aren't half bad. I mean yeah, if you look at various objects individually they are pretty crappy, but if you look at the picture as a whole it actually looks pretty good. Better than titles launching at comparable cost and even above. Weater effects and day/night are present.
Combat is simplistic but offers you options. The game doesn't have player skills, instead some gear has skills attached (for a max or 3 at a time it seems). So switching up the gear switches up the skills. So far I'm not bored of it. I just wished the energy would regen otherwise my chars are going to sleep more than humanly possible.

This might be one of the hardest games I have tried to review so far, as far as pros and cons go.
The art style is very well done--a mash-up of cartoon mixed with very surreal objects and environments.  It is quite an engaging atmosphere to traverse as you go from each distinctly different room to the next.
You start in a cage and you are on your own from there.  It can be rather daunting trying to figure out what you are supposed to do, even from the get go, and you are going to be doing a lot of random clicking on objects that are both identified by a cursor change to let you know that an object is intended to be used or picked up, as well as interactive objects that you are offered no cursor change to signify whether or not it is something that can be used, picked up, or perhaps intended to later be used as part of the seemingly random puzzles that each room offers.  There will be lots of orbs that you pick up, with no explanation whether these are merely collectables (which they are as it turns out, so far as I have noticed--I am just past the first "part" of the game) or "inventory objects" for puzzles.
If you don't mind thinking WAY outside of the box and relying mainly on experimentation (or a walkthrough) than this game has a lot to offer.  It breaks the traditional mold of a point and click adventure game, and I have yet to decide whether this is a good thing or a bad thing.  I, personally, enjoy both point and click adventure games as well as hidden object games, and I grew up playing all of those silly Sierra and Lucasarts games that had you often using item in unexpected ways, so the culmination that is Violett is overall appealing to me.  It certainly won't be for everyone, but if you can pick it up cheap or in a bundle somewhere, it is definately worth taking a look at.  There is something very luring about the abstract areas that you explore, and while some parts are hair-pullingly frustrating, other parts cannot help but make you smile and want to see where else this odd game is going to take you.

Despite the constant negative reviews for this game, i have been around since the open beta and have since purchased the season pass and have continued to play since. There are definitely a fair amount of bugs and other things that might steer someone away from buying this game, but I can personally back this game as someone who has generally disliked ubisoft as a company for a long time.
Starting with the pros, for honor has to have one of the best combat systems i've ever seen for a game of its kind, that is a medieval style fighting game. It is easy to learn, and the design makes it easy to see even while staring your opponent(s) down. The simplicity of the basic controls, being blocking, parrying, gaurd breaking, dodging and so on, make it so that if you learn these basic mechanics you can pick up any hero and perform well. This is good for players who want to pick up multiple heroes, because it serves as a backbone to each character before learning the specific playstyles, abilities, and differences of each character.
Graphics wise it is definitely impressive which is to be expected of a game from a major company. The animation is realistic and believable (Though being a fighting game some things can seem a little weird to do in a sword fight, like headbutting and obviously telegraphed overhead strikes. It is definitely not meant to realistically simulate medieval warfare, it is more inspired and fantastical than a game like Chivalry or Mount and Blade.) It is easy to become immersed in the game, especially given all the customizations to truly personalize your warrior.
The ongoing territorial war between the three factions can bring about a good sense of pride for whatever team you fought for. Knights won the beta, vikings wrecked season 1, and it seems as though the knights are back for seconds, leaving the wee- samurai in the dust. But as they've shown before, wee- samurai rage can quickly overcome even two factions at once, so keep an eye on the little buggers. At first glance it may not seem like your individual contributions make a difference, and when you don't assign your assets yourself, they really kinda don't. When you focus on a territory, i have seen my contributions raise the level of influence on said territory myself. And in the last few updates of a round or season, you REALLY see the momentum increase. All in all it's a fun little side gig to contribute to. and if you win you get the bragging rights and a shiny golden border and ornament! (stupid neckbeards and their shiny golden pizza shields..)
On the other hand, there are two major problems I can see with this game.
First, the community has become increasingly horrid on the PC. I would mostly blame this on the reddit for encouraging circlejerks and saltfests about how overpowered x hero is, or how x hero is "ruining the game." The community has arguably driven ITSELF to such a small number. All that seems to be left are the ones who have been around since the beginning, with no signs of new players. To make matters worse, what little new players i see are so quickly trash talked and belittled for not being as good as the veterans and while i'm always game for a little trash talk, there comes a point where being hazed by a 4 man group for simply PICKING YOUR FAVORITE HERO can be very discouraging. Ubi definitely needs to promote this game with a free weekend or a large sale and get the community on the same level as the console ones.
Secondly, the connections. Earlier on it was pretty horrendous, but in my near 350 hours i have experienced very few connection problems. The majority of it is stopping mid game to migrate hosts and resync players and that's understandable, while other times it will flat out end the game and bring you back to the main menu. What people think the solution is, is dedicated servers. There are problems with this, being latency and more frequent lag. While it does have its problems i will say i have only blamed a death on lag a handful of times. I would say peer to peer is the way to go for this game. It IS how Modern warfare 2 did it, and it was regarded as one of the best games of its time.
All in all, i've fallen in love with this game, and i haven't even kept up with it since it was announced. I was convinced by the open beta that it stood out as a ubisoft game, and the devs are clearly trying their best, though they could be doing more. For Honor has really filled a specific need of mine in gaming. The rewarding and satisfying executions for purely outplaying your opponent is never old to watch, the pride in whatever faction you choose, all memes aside, they're all super awesome and badass in their own ways (deus vult). I would wholeheartledly reccomend giving this game a chance. Perhaps not at full price, but it's a steal if it goes on sale. Hopefully if a free weekend comes along, definitely give it a shot, pick up a hero and put some time into it and decide if it's for you. And if you ever need someone to crusade with, you know who to call ;^)

It’s an amazing amusing little game with somewhat charming and nostalgic graphics and music. It is crime that this game is free — I want to buy it.
You can call this game “one-stick healer”: you play as a princess wandering through the little world populated only with ill creatures. And you are healing them with magic in an one-stick shooter sequences. It’s very short but nice, charming and a little nostalgic experience. Hell, I have spent more time writing this review than clearing the game (~1.0 hour), and you've probably spent more time reading reviews, when you can just play the damn game instead (it free).
Gameplay: You wander around a small world, open chests and heal different characters. Healing is simple: after a small dialog with an ill NPC, you will appear in the arena with enemies and obstacles. Objectives: do not die, dodge bullets and shoot every enemy. During healing sequences the princess is always shooting where she is directed at, making it a "one stick shooter". It's a little tricky and you should always keep it in mind. When everything (except you) is dead, NPC is healed. And after you defeated the final boss you can marry them.
Story: go to the Hurtland, practice your healing skills and find yourself a husband (or wife).
Character: In the end, you can marry every-bloody-thing and get an exclusive ending for it. Which is lovely.

Over the Top Zombie Action that tries desparately to satisfy everyone. Nevertheless I enjoy my time with RE6.
The controls are sometimes messy, textures washedout and there are way to many superfluous one liners.....but Ada and Leon grow on me since way back.
Capcom put a lot of content in this game, 4 campaigns each 5-7 hours, different game modes and serving a large-scale story that is..... maybe too big for its own good...but hey! it kept me busy and I was never bored.

Well, It's a good action game, pretty much like RE5 was, tough much of the complaints about the game are exactly about that. It no longer feels like a "Resident Evil" game to be honest (even less so than RE5), but that doesn't mean it's bad, it's actually pretty fun. The 3 different campaigns change things up quite a bit in terms of ambience: Leon's is a little bit slower paced, similar to RE4, Jake's is more like RE5, and Chris's is much more action oriented. The 3 play pretty much the same, but they "feel" different, and that's good. There's also a 4th campaign with Ada, which is probably the best one since it feels more like old-school RE than any other thing in RE6.
Weapons and inventory systems are poorly designed, just like the ones in RE5. They're functional, but they could've done a better job at it. Weapon customization is gone, replaced by a skills system, which is not too bad, but you don't feel as involved in it as in previous games... you just select a few passives and that's it. Combat is much improved, with more mobility for characters and ways to dodge enemy attacks. Play as Chris and you might think a mutant with a rocket launcher would be worse than regular zombies, but play as Leon and you'll see how dangerous zombies can be. Overall, it's a very entertaining game. The plot is fine, it's great to see some familiar faces again, and the new ones are interesting enough to justify maybe a sequel with only them, who knows. Monsters are varied and fun, and mosts levels offer a decent challenge, and are varied enough too.
Mercenaries is no doubt the best of the series, and once you finish every campaign, it'll probably be a good time sink if you're into it. Here is more evident than ever where the new combat features shine. And about multiplayer... almost nobody plays anything else other than Mercenaries, the DLC modes are empty all the time, so they're not worth getting, since you need people to play them with and no one ever does. Integration with
doesn't solve that, sadly. Co-op is nice, and not nearly as annoying as it was in RE5. That being said, in the single player campaign, your partner is actually helpful, not a burden like before.
For all old Resident Evil fans, my recommendation would be to treat this game as something else, based on the world of Resident Evil. In the story, over the years things have been escalating, and now everything everywhere is messed up, not just a Mansion/Precint/Small Town, so it's hard to think how we could get back those slow, scary and suspenseful moments from previous games. I know Revelations tried, but if feels dated and comparably too slow and shallow. You'll find some of that tense vibe here tough (with Leon and Ada, and sometimes Jake), but not that often. For anyone else, just try it, it's a fun experience. As an action game, it's great.
Mercenaries in RE6 is one of the best and in-depth score attack modes out there, and as a bonus you get a campaign mode where Leon attempts driving a car.

On the whole, this game is best enjoyed with another player running co-op with you through the campaigns. Graphics are very well done, weapons are detailed and sound fantastic. Voice acting is mediocre on some characters but absolutely stunning on others. Interface can be clunky due to the obvious port from console version. This can occasionally cause movement issues where the camera locks in a certain angle that makes your directional movement very unintuitive. Not really a huge deal except for quick time action sequences that involve running toward/away from the camera; can be frustrating during these times. Otherwise, the controls are effective, not too hard to get used to and the melee combat is surprisingly solid and satisfying.

At first, I did not really like what I was playing, so I was thinking of just stop playing. The camera is so zoomed in, it kind of hurt my eyes. It is true, the game is actually pretty radically different from the previous Resident Evil games, as the game is no longer a survival horror like it used to be. But.... I think Resident Evil 6 is still in a way, a survival horror game still, kind of. There are basically tons of zombies that you can kill, but you do not really get much of ammo in the game. Meaning it is necessary to save ammunition and just keep running. The stages are huge, especially the Leon's story, and it is basically recommended to just run rather than dealing with those zombies one by one. I thought it was kind of interesting, because I guess this is a little more realistic than having to deal with every zombie that you encounter. The control has gotten better and I did not really find much of issues with it. As many have complained, QTE happens a lot in this game, but I am not sure. I don't think it was "that" bad, as you still get the chance to redo that part right away even if you die anyway. And many people also complained about the difficulty of the game being too hard even on normal. I am not sure if the game has gone through some radical changes with the updates (I know it did for camera), and this might be the reason why I do not really find this game that bad. The game is certainly playable and enjoyable from start to finish. For someone like me who likes Call of Duty style action a lot, Resident Evil 6 is certainly the game that I can recommend to any action game fans. Not every RE fan would find this game fun, but it was good enough for me. Good stories and beautiful endings for Leon, Chris and Jake, too. I didn't really bother with Ada's story, as it is kind of boring. Overall, great game. Looking forward to Resident Evil 7.

For my First Review of 2015, the first game I've passed in 2015: Violett
Violett is a very pretty game. The Backgrounds are lovely, colourful & have an Alice in Wonderland meets Honey I shrunk the kids sort of charm. It is a point and click adventure with a cute story waiting to get out.
Unfortunately the story never really does get out. There is little narrative in any form of presentation, verbal or non verbal and even less direction. The titular young girl has some telekinetic powers which seem to be limited to the very specific items the creators did not feel like animating while other times you can practically reach an item you need but have to float a ladder over to it to climb up and retrieve it. Where are her mind powers there?
The other abilities are only used to bypass a couple of road-block hazards which themselves are only blocking collection items. One of these skills is a floating power, kind of a limited flight, which is only used in maybe three instances and yet in the many other situations where it would be a big help in reaching some place it is somehow imposable for her to use.
If this had been part platformer these abilities would have been a lot of fun to play with but as it stands they seem to be just tacked on to again cut down on animation.
That said I, having studied animation myself, understand how much time and tedium can be involved in seeming simple motions so I do not blame the creators for that trick.
Pros : Easy to pick up and play
Pretty to look at
Often available for next to nothing.
Cons: Like a lot of point and click games, the puzzles are less about intellect and more about noticing what piece of the background is a different shade or makes the arrow become a hand.
Little story development.
A lot of very slow moving to and from-ing.
Pick it up on sale if you like point and click, don't if you don't

Violett. Admittedly, this is a tough one. I adored the music, the art style (the 2.5D in-game, not the 2D intro/ending), the colorful characters, the bug world, and the goals. I'm a fan of puzzle games and "collect-them-all" type of scavenger hunts, and I rarely have difficulty completing them on my own.
However I simply could not complete Violett without a walkthrough. Many of the puzzles are
convoluted, and that's
from the main 4 required for the
achievement. The roof elevator puzzle alone nearly made me weep and ragequit.
Even "simpler" puzzles are not at all intuitive. They could take hours of trial and error, especially:
- If you miss a necessary item that you can only get in another scene (but you aren't told where);
- If you move to one side of the screen, the scene elements can block the very thing you need to click on (e.g. the Kitchen &
achievement, or any number of orbs that are hidden from certain angles);
- Any instance of "nope, can't have this/get there till you do this/find that/give this character X number of these";
- If you don't figure out the specific puzzle mechanics or "logic", which are rarely or never explained.
I'm not saying games should hold your hand through puzzles. That wouldn't present any challenge. But when the clues and/or a solution to a puzzle are so COMPLETELY off-the-wall and nothing you'd even think to try without tripping over it accidentally -- that's just bad foresight in the puzzle design itself.
And then there are the doors. Oh god, the doors. Go in here, come out there. Go back in the same way, come out on a different level. Rinse, repeat. It's like a damn Benny Hill hallway chase scene, except you're the only one running around like a loon. Oh, and even worse, if you pull a lever/push a button in those scenes, every route changes and you have to figure it all out again. *facepalm*
I do wish the characters had a bit more interesting/interactive elements instead of just being part of the scene or spouting chimpmunk-speed gibberish (sounded like Russian at some points) along with a single picture bubble as a "clue", but that limitation didn't really take away from [mostly] understanding what they wanted from you.
You WILL need a guide if you're going for the
achievement to collect all the orbs. Some of them are so hidden away it's like the devs don't
you to find things unless you click every spot on the screen. At least there aren't any click penalties, cuz man, would I be in trouble.
So why do I recommend the game?
Aside from the frustrations of the puzzles, I would still say Violett is a unique and fun experience. I didn't really mind using a text or video walkthrough for
most parts, because I could look past that and enjoy other aspects of the game, like the art, character design, "2.5D" level design, and silly Alice-like atmosphere. If you have no issues with "reading the directions" and then just enjoying it while you follow them, you may get the same level of enjoyment out of Violett that I did.
It's not a masterpiece by any definition, but even after a complete playthrough my mind drifts back to Violett's bug world now and again, and in that sense I would say the game is pleasantly unforgettable.
I wouldn't get it at full price (mainly because the insane puzzle designs waste far more playtime than they should), but when it's on sale (especially for .99 cents), you should consider giving it a shot.

Violett bridges the gap between classic point&click and the causal gaming 'busy picture' genre, and tries to make more use of touch functionality doing so.
The art is fantastic, the story bits are funny and contain great humor. The character design is one really neat piece (I love that snails :D), and the fantasy-setting Violett finds herself in is a refreshing approach to the genre. There are one or two translation errors in the found diary pages, but since they are 'only' flavortext, this does not matter much.
The puzzles are nicely tailored and make sense most of the time, but this is where my ranting starts.
The logic of the riddles is not very consistant leaving the player to simply grab unreachable objects by magic in one case, and completely ignoring this ability in another, similar case. Also there are some timing-based riddles, where you need to hit the right spot at the right time. The Bossfight - just so much: collect as much of those 'orbs' as possible, you will need them.
Especially the 'dynamic' puzzles and the 'swipe' mechanic might feel pretty alien to someone who is used to point and clicks, but I recon it a worthy experiment.
All in all the game is not as frustrating as it seems to be, it's not too short… just a nice, and really sweet looking short story.

I bought this game on a whim because it was on sale, and I'm glad I did. The puzzles can also be challenging, but the game lets you buy hints, which is a plus for those who are and aren't good at puzzles. So yeah, I think this game is good.

Point and click games generally have three factors that determine its quality: story, art style, and puzzles.
This game has a rather simplistic straightforward story, so don't expect any plot twists, internal conflicts, or multiple endings. In addition, even though the story is largely derivative of Lewis Caroll's
, the diary pages do provide some interesting and amusing backstory to the characters that you meet along the way.
In terms of art style,
has some very pleasing hand painted 2D background art and the 3D models are not too shabby either. Also, don't fret about turning this game's graphical quality up to the highest. It barely causes the fan of my low end graphics card to spin faster.
Finally, the puzzles and challenges of this game aren't too difficult provided that one has a keen eye in spotting patterns and hidden clues. Also, the game has a hint system for those that are stuck on a particular puzzle. Of course, if you choose to use it you won't qualify for certain achievements.
Overall, this is a point and click game is with an emphasis on puzzles and challenges. If one is looking for something akin to the
or
, then one isn't going to find it here in this game.

This game, while it is limited from a gameplay perspective, can really draw you in if you are like me and love games that have an investigational aspect to them.  In the early parts the game holds your hand a bit too much for my taste, it loosens its hold a bit in the later parts.
Story is where the game really shines, however.  You play as the administrator to some Orwellian Big Brother type system used by the Government to spy on citizens suspected of Crimes (sort of a social media detective).  Tapping phone lines, e-mails, getting into people's personal computers, etc.
I found myself becomming quite engaged by the characters, which is impressive if you consider you never have any direct intereactions with them besides spying on them.  Still as I went about my investigations I found myself feeling a nawing sense of guilt for violating the privacy of these characters to try and get at the Suspect I needed to catch.  That alone says something about the quality of the writing in the game.
I would highly recommend this game if you like a heavily story driven game, especially for only $10.  It's a unique experience that immersed me to the point where I was having actual emotional reactions to the story and characters.

When PC gaming first began, the genre at its head was the point and click adventure game. For years, games like King's Quest, Gabriel Knight, and The Curse of Monkey Island dominated the market. There were so many point and click games, every single idea one could have became used and abused, and the genre faded into one of gaming years past.
JazzPunk is not your typical point and click adventure game.
Firstly, it employs a clever mix of the classic Commodore 64 games and more modern shooters, giving you a game that feels like a shooter and plays like a classic. In addition, it has an abundance of something that just wasn't present in early games in the genre, and that's personality. The game will leave you holding your sides in its hilarious nonsense time and time again. Throw in a clever and unique art direction along side a perfect soundtrack, and you've got yourself the masterpiece that is JazzPunk.
Despite this praise, Jazzpunk is not without fault. The biggest one is this: Its combination of floaty controls, psychedelic graphics, and low FoV will leave many users nauseous after just a few minutes of play. It can be a risky endeavor, play this game at your own risk. Another issue is that this game is quite short. for $15, you can find yourself beating this game in less than an hour. This may seem to be a ridiculous complaint to fans of The Stanley Parable, who know that for the same price you can finish the game in 20 minutes, but the fun in The Stanley Parable comes from its replay value. This game is all about exploration, but one can end their experience in a short amount of time, and there aren't 17 more endings to choose from. If one were to plan on buying this game, they need to be patient and search for secrets, otherwise they could be looking at a 45 minute game rather than a 4 hour one.
All in all, JazzPunk is a creative and interesting experience. It blends unique game design with witty and pleasurable humor, but can be dangerous to users who are prone to epilepsy or motion sickness, as well as being a tad on the short side.

Get this game. Play with friends. That's the short version.
Long version:
While this game is one that really doesn't get the love it actually deserves, considering all the ideas that were thrown in for the multiplayer co-op. For starters, the game controls great, which goes well with the action-based gameplay it has. (Kinda like RE5, but actually faster and kinda more fluent) Each Story and the characters get their own weapon load outs, enemies and... well story.
Basically Leon's storyline is fighting actual zombies. Not the kind of zombies you encountered in RE5, i mean actual skeleton, undead, slowmoving (Well, some are fast, but attack pretty slow) zombies, like people are used to. Leon's "ability" is to be able to dual-weild hand guns, and Helena's is to do an dodge-shoot attack with her starting shotgun.
Chris's story is, you could say, squad-based, for  some chapters, you are aided by NPC Army characters, which i guess helps for people who are new to the game. But the enemies are Ja'vo which are zombies that can morph, can use guns, are fast, etc.
Then we have Jake's story. It's kinda like Chris's story in terms of enemies, but there is no NPCs helping you. I should also note, while it's pretty weird for Resident evil, Jake and Sherry are pretty much great melee characters. Jake uses his bare fists, but geez is he awesome in hand to had combat! And Sherry has a stun rod which can let you lead up with an action attack which can take multiple enemies down or instant kill one enemy. And it CAN prevent enemies from morphing with it as well. Which surprisingly can be fun if you actually know how to use it correctly! And no, that doesn't mean they are any worse with guns than anyone else, but it helps alot for when you run out of ammo, which can happen alot when playing on Professional mode.
And then there is Ada. Now what's different about Ada's story: First off, its a story you play on your own, without a CPU controlling a friendly character. HOWEVER, if you decide to play co-op, it'll let you control an "Agent", i guess from Operation Raccoon City? I'm not entirely sure. But its nice to know that you don't HAVE to play it alone. Anyway, in her story, it includes some old resident evil style puzzles to complete to progress the game. And as you go through the story, you get a behind the scenes look at what she was doing during the storylines of every character's story and how she actually had an impact on said storylines, so you should only play her story once you do everyone else's story.
Then here are the cool ideas they had with this game:
For starters, you can actually play a mode called "Agent Hunt", where you invade a player's storyline as a zombie. And trust me, THIS makes the game SO MUCH MORE INTERESTING! For example, from an experience of mine, during a boss battle with a chainsaw weilding zombie, two players had invaded my game as zombies, and they would either try to set me up in a way so it would be easy for the chainsaw zombie to kill me OR fail doing so and get chainsawed in the process. So during the entire fight, i am dodging the players and trying to defeat the boss. Not to mention that because i was playing in professional, the player's attack speed is slightly faster and have a higher chance of morph into a stronger zombie and attempt to kill me.
So yea, you play as a zombie and your objective is to kill a player and make their life IMPOSSIBLE. But fear not, you can turn this option off and have no players join your game as a zombie, but i highly suggest leaving this on for a challenge.
Then we have Story Intersections. During the story of the characters, they sometimes end up finding eachother where they all try to defeat a boss or get to an objective together. What's great about this is that if another player is playing the story of the OTHER characters and ends up at the intersection story, all four players end up doing the boss battle together. Sometimes it's one pair of characters aiding another pair, all 4 players fighting a boss or, in Ada's case, have 3 players fight bosses or have her use special vehicles.
Then there's the extra modes, which i actually can't talk much about... sadly its because not many players actually play them, even thought some of them actually sound pretty much. Such as one of them has one player playing as the boss character from Jake's story vs other players using the main characters. Then there's Deathmatch which isn't really exciting with RE6 mechanics, mainly because the second you get shot, you are basically screwed. Note, some of these are DLC.
Then we have Mercenaries, which isn't actually DLC, is where you play a large swarm of zombies, score-attack kind of thing. Again, you can play on your own or with a friend. And as a Steam exclusive, you get to play as Left4Dead2 characters.
All in all, if you have a friend, i highly recommend grabbing this game and play it in Co-op.

What went wrong here? Well, everything.
The gameplay, arguably the most important part of most if not any game, is broken. The camera, which was allegedly fixed shortly after the console release, is still broken. Basically, it jerks you around every time you are trying to do anything. When you are running, the camera pulls back and views everything from the low vantage point. Basically, it makes you NOT see your surroundings pretty well. When you try to melee someone, it pulls your forward and then in all different directions.
Another thing, Dead Space 3 introduced the roll option. I barely used it and didn't like it much. DS2 worked perfectly fine without it. However, all you needed to do was use your WSAD keys along with the SPACE key to pick which way you wanted to roll. Pretty easy. Not in this game. If you want to roll left, click Z. If you want to roll right, click C. If you want to roll back, click X. If you want to roll/slide forward, click 2. Convenient, huh? Don't bother using it, because when you divert one of your fingers to try to roll left or right you will expose yourself to harm by not being able to use WSAD effectively because you only have 5 fingers.
I also had to turn brightness all the way up. Why? Well, evidently folks at CAPCOM were creating this game for consoles without PC in mind. So when you are walking in a dark environment and looking straight you see that 'dark fog' slowly lifting up revealing everything (like in the good old days on PS1). THEN, all of a sudden you see a zombie 3 feet away that jumps you. WHY? WHY? WHY? WHY?
Should I mention there are re-spawning enemies in most areas? Should I mention how frustrating it is when you try to make a pathway for your partner but the enemies keep respawning behind you while your partner is running out of bullets since it takes good 10-15 to turn that wheel and lower the bridge? Hell, they also have respawning enemies on a falling airplane!
Also, two people pushing a 20 ton rock boulder?
Yeah, Count me out.
One of the most annoying things in this game is the jumping zombies. Yeah, one second they are slowly walking towards you and another moment they are flying towards you with their arms open. Then they knock you down which is when you have to press WSAD keys all over the place to get them off. However, while doing so your health will STILL DRAIN. Oh, and another thing about health. This is how you heal. You first combine green and red herbs by pressing R in the small menu, when you figure out how to do that you have to look at the bottom right to see how many pills you have. The amount of pills = the amount of health bars. If you want to use it then click 1 three times. Yeah, I know, it's totally idiotic. Try to figure that out during battle. Better yet, try to figure out how to use the spray quickly. 4 hours into the game and I still had trouble healing myself quickly because the menus ARE CLUNKY AND BROKEN.
There are so many other negatives in this games. The more I played it, the worse it got. I thought about RE5 and just how much more superior it was to this game. RE5 graphics were better for one thing and that was 5 years ago. RE5 had directx10, a semi-bearable story, better refined gameplay, cool environments, decent textures, worked out physics (shooting with a shotgun actually meant 3-4 zombies flying back), plenty of hidden treasures, etc. Each enemy required some kind of accuracy and finesse. In RE6 however you just punch zombies to death, and even THAT doesn't always work. If you have one health left your punches don't mean a thing and your screen flashes constantly with the white and red vomit inducing in-nauseating glow. And when you or your partner gets knocked down your screen flashes for 2 seconds with white and red so that you can't see anything. THEN, right after that you try to figure out who exactly got knocked down, your partner or you? I KID YOU NOT.
Btw. why does Ada Wong look Caucasian? She definitely did a nose job. Perhaps Capcom was hoping to attract more Western players or something?
Oh, did I also mention that cutscenes during boss battles don't leave you immune from small enemies? Yeah. Let's say you are fighting a boss and then they show a mid-battle cutscene, you WILL get hurt by a nearby zombie during that time.
One of the mistakes they made is give you the ability to punch, kick and kick in mid air after running (Like in Double Dragon). Which is a yet another insult to the series. Another mistake is giving you the ability to punch ANYTIME you want, and not just when there is a dazzled foe in front of you. So you may just end up spamming the punch button all over the place until you basically clubber the zombie into the oblivion. If you do a finishing move and there is a zombie that's swinging a shovel at you then you WILL get hit right after your finishing move.
There's no more $ that you collect and use towards purchasing weapons and upgrades anymore. Noooo, they scrapped all that. Now you pick up "skill points" after slain enemies and then and then and then....Oh that's right, when do I use those skill points towards upgrading my character? Umm, NEVER in the game. (I was playing on the highest difficulty so maybe that's why, but regardless). You have to quit the game and go into main menu, click campaign and then click SKILL POINTS. And then you have about 30 skills or perks to buy and upgrade and only 3 SLOTS to put them in. This is useless. You can't buy any weapons, you will find a few extra though but you will still be using your main beginning pistols for most of the campaign.
Anyways, I am sure more things will come up. I just can't think of every single idiotic point about this game so I will keep updating this review.
I don't know what else to say. I felt a lot of hate from Capcom. I felt that I was being punished for something. It seems like they made this installment simply because it was that time to make another RE game.
