First off I really like atmospheric games. Survival, post-apocalyptic, seemed real interesting project. As bonus there were talks like "spiritual successor to S.T.A.L.K.E.R" and "some guys from GSC Games are working on this".
Game is fun for first few hours, learning stuff and when you get the grasp of it... that's it. Then you will realize there is nothing about survival or post-apocalyptic or "stalker-ish" except visuals. Don't let the map design and leather jacket fool you. Wrong tags Vostok Games, wrong tags.
What is actually in game - 8v8 small maps. You rush, do your "PRA PRA PRA" and chow on your medkits until you die. Respawn after 15 seconds, repeat. Later edge in game is throwing scanner to see enemies on minimap, throw smoke grenade, circle back to base to replenish supplies. There are few game modes, but its all practically the same. Your Faction does not matter on battlefield in terms "who vs who", so you can be in team with guys form all factions vs similar team. "You are mercenary."
Weapons are so "balanced" in Tiers(1-5) that all of them feels like waterpistols. Lacks feeling of impact, floats around, but maybe that is just me. I guess it is weird to expect♥♥♥♥♥♥to get ♥♥♥♥ed up if I shoot it with rifle. SMG's have range of 20-30 meters, rifles have range 40 meters, after that bullets do way less damage, multiple headshots wont drop anyone. All weapons are made to do "PRA PRA PRA", not do what they are supposed to do within their role. Don't even think going in high tier with starting weapon, it will be airsoft gun, despite using same ammunition as top tier guns. There are terms like "damage per second" and "time to kill", so don't expect satisfying gunplay.
All weapons can be fitted with scopes, grips, silencers. Which is really nice, until you see every guy running around with sights, silencers, grips and lazer pointers in this "post-apocalyptic" world. Even Makarov can be fitted with red dot sight. However you will not buy or get attachments in any way. Instead magical Survarium Fairy will give it to you when you kill particular amount of players with it and only for that specific gun. Kills required is not small number, on end tiers its even in thousands.
There are 4 "Factions" that can sell you equipment for ingame currency. After joining one you get Reputation with that faction, start at "Tier 1" and go all the way up, buy better gear and play higher tier games. You can change faction at any time, but it takes long to gain reputation. So plan ahead, check out gear of all factions, make informed decision. You will want to get weapons you like, but DON'T DO THAT. Get weapons with best stats, there is no resemblance with real-life weapons, only name and skin. Don't get attached to your weapon, in next tier it is going to suck.
There are no economy or trade of any kind within players, you get equipment from Factions, weekly Treasure Hunt gambling, Daily quest or buy them for Gold(real money). So you can't give your old AK to a friend.
You can enchant(yes, enchant, not upgrade, because it is magic) your gear by throwing "spare parts"(another ingame currency) at your gear, there is 50/50 chance that it will stick. Rather than going to the usual stream of short un informative "down vote reviews." I am going to try to explain basic game mechanics, recent updates and what the game does well and what its shortcoming are.
TL;DR : Game is good.
Firstly the game uses 2 leveling systems: a general level which nets you a skill point for perks, of which there are currently 3 perk trees to choose from. Firearms, Physique and Knowlege of the Forest.
- Firearms is pretty self explanatory; passively increasing weapon handling skills.
- Physique/Physical deals with sprint duration and regeneration, movespeed and weight limit, and a grenade throw distance and fall damage reduction.
- Knowledge of the Forest; now this is where its gets interesting. A core focus of the game is with randomly spawning "Anomalies" or if your a STALKER fan "Artifacts," little gems or rocks with law defying affects. The skill tree works with resisting the Anomalies initial damaging aura to utilizing their abilities.
Now to the 2nd level system the Factions.
Being there are 4 Factions currently.
Each faction having an assortment of weapons and armor that are only available to them, I'll give a brief descriptioin for each:
Scavengers - pretty much a general mix of close to long range weapons with mostly light armor with a little heavy armor available to them.
Black Market - Similar scheme to Scavengers in their armor, but a more pronounced close range weaponry.
Renaissance Army - A lot of Heavy armor and and excels at meduim range with their nice selection of Assault rifles and LMGs.
And lastly the Fringe Settlers - Longer range weaponry and alot of light armor, but with a twist, having better synergy with Artifacts.
Moving on to the recent big updates
Most recent update has halved faction levels from 10 to 5 teirs, making unlocking weapons and equipment a little faster as well as condencing the player base. And added set bonuses to some armors.
Changes to FOV when aiming down sights with weapons as how close the weapon's sights are to the camera and also some weapons had a their sight's architecture changed allowing less obstruction while aiming down the sights.
Gameplay.
Pretty much like every other 1st person Shooter with Arena style maps. With sprinting, grenades, mines. but unlike most FPS games, Survarium has more nuanced gun control requirements; being some guns have a need to pace your shots, as their recoil kicks the sights around.
And the aforementioned Artifacts, these objects randomly generate throughout maps, starting out as little glowing spheres of light on the ground; once they fully manifest they will generate an aura around them that aggressively damages players within their field ( damage can be reduced through the Knowledge skill tree and some armor pieces having higher anomaly protection, and limited oxygen pack equipment can negate damage out right but with high weight)
Ailments
Guns do most of the damage but most of the time, you're gonna die to bleeding out
Artifacts
so far there are 4 different Artifacts in the game. each artifact has a passive effect on the player and with the acquirement of a Perk, can be activated for a much higher effect for a limited time. Another thing to remember is to pick up an Artifact you MUST have an equipment with a "Artifact Container" attribute
So we have:
Sponge - this orange/ brown porous rock generates a poisonous cloud when it fully matures, that lingers even after you leave its field of effect. when picked up it grants a passive resistance to other poisonous anomalies and artifacts (I'll be honest, this one lost alot of use, when they removed the different Map's anomalies effects) But when activated it can be thrown like a grenade releasing a cloud of poisonous spores that also obscure view, like a smoke grenade.
Larkspur: this blue flower also generates a poisnous field around itself, but once acquired it will give a passive health regen and when activated it will give a massive surge of health regen, almost instant, really.
Spring: Weird Pink planet Saturn looking crystal, generates a radiation effect. When picked up, will grant a slight move speed buff. and once actived will grant a greater move speed buff coupled with a decent Stamina regen buff.
Onyx: and lastly (for now, at least) this Black crystal shaped rock in some sort of tray will grant you a slight passive bullet resistance and when activated grants you 50% damage mitigation (I think)
Equipment - Guns and Armor
Armor foremost as it has a range of customization possibilities, Chest and Pants both can have a reskin and 2 decals/patchs. reskins ranging through different textures to camos you can either buy them with gold premium currency or unlock them through achievements.
And now the bread and butter of any Gun game. We got Pistols to Sniper Rifles, Carbines to Assault Rifles and my personal favorite, Shotguns. each weapon has a sequence of attachments that are unlocked by the number of kills you get with that weapon and has the ability to equip 3 modifiers that can change their stats
And did I mention Grenades? Well, not just grenades. Medkits to syringes with buffs
Pay to Win?
No, not really. You can purchase premium currency, to buy some special weapons and armor pieces, but each purchase is given, the 3, random modifiers, so its a gamble to get good set of modifiers for each piece.
and gun and armor mod require Spare Parts and Silver (Gold premium) Although silver currency only gives you a 50% chance to successfuly make a mod, Gold at 100% (yeah, its a free to play game, remember?)
You can only get Spare Parts after matches or a big amount as a reward in the Weekly Treasure Hunt, with the Treasure Cache Map item (2 free each week)
Gold can also be used to purchase slight player buffs, but these buffs can be acquired with Artifact use and some equipment
Bots
yes there are AI bots in the game, pretty much a drag in Team deathmatch for both teams. but are quite directionless in the other 3 objective based game modes.
Game Modes
4 game modes for now.
Team Death match is pretty basic, 2 teams with a life pool /tickets that depletes with each death. which ever reaches 0 first loses or has less at the end of the time limit, also loses.
Research: 3 static, strong points on the Map are capturable, which ever team reaches 100% first wins
Battery Retrieval: Around 4 or so static points on the map randomly generate a big car battery, that needs to be carried back to your team's spawn, while you carry the battery you move slower and cannot shoot or do any other action ( I think you can Jump, though). You will aslo be revealed on the map. So, have your teammates cover you. (Or they might just shoot you and take the battery themselves, but not always. Just slight of times.)
Artifact Hunt: Favorite Game mode this one. 2 teams positioning themselves waiting for the Artifact to be announced and revealed on the map, and the subsequent shoot out that insues after, to pick up the Artifact. When picked up you gain a decent health regen, just above that of Larkspur's passive. at the cost of reduced movespeed. And you can shoot while carrying it (And you dont need any Artifact Container equipment to pick it up)
Now with all that covered, I do find the game to have Drawbacks as well. Currently Matchmaking is a littlefaster but the majority of game still consist of 3 players and the rest of Bots per team. More on the AI even though they appear to be wondering aimlessly, dont let that fool you into thinking they are harmless, as soon as your first shot rings out, they will almost immediate get a fix on you, so be more patient and get a headshot on them. and depending on what gear set they are generated with they can be down right infuriating to deal with, A bot with the Scavenger Sniper gear set will quick scope you, etc.

I used to love this game as a kid, it was so much fun. Is it as good as I remember? Well, no. Is it still fun? Yes.
It's a simple enough game. Eat smaller fish, grow bigger, eat the previously bigger but now smaller fish. I finished the game in about 8 hours, however I did take a lot of breaks inbetween levels to go do other stuff. And while I did lose all my lives, I didn't lose all my continues. By the time I got to the last level I was on my last continue. However, this isn't really because the game is super challenging, so to say.
One of the main flaws with this game for me is that it's pretty frustrating, and rather unfair at times. When you have a screen that's zoomed in on your big fish it's kind of hard to tell what's around you. One wrong move and you end up in the mouth of a giant fish you had no clue was even there, and by the time you see it it's too late. While this issue isn't present in the whole game, it's still there, making it so you can lose your lives in pretty unfair ways late in the game.
The story is simple and kid-friendly, and if you're just looking for a little bit of fun for a couple of hours, then go ahead and pick this up I guess. However, I'm not sure that this game will click with everybody. I grew up playing these kinds of Popcap games on my dad's computer. Playing this is like getting slapped in the face with a nostalgia fish.
I've also bought this game at least 3 times by now, I think. I have honestly lost count, because I always lost those codes Popcap would give you when buying it from them. Definitely a lot easier when doing it on Steam!
Now, would I recommend this game? I'm not sure, to be completely honest, as I'm writing this. You've probably already seen whether or not that thumb is pointing up and down. Even though I did enjoy it, I'm not sure if most people who didn't grow up playing this and the original would, which is why I can't say I recommend it.
However, if you think this game looks fun and you think you'd enjoy it, then go ahead and try it out. It doesn't cost a lot, so it's not like you have a whole lot to lose.

I would definitely recommend this game if you like an outstanding story, sci-fi and non-combat games. It will suck you in and you will be scared at times.

The protaginist goes by the name of Simon Jarret.
The story starts with you going to a doctor to get a brain scan after you have been in an accident. You lose consciousness  and later wake up in an unknown place.  You later find out that the place you find yourself at is a underwater facility known by the name of PATHOS - II. Throughout the story you will question what it means to be human and the boundary between Human and Machine. You will learn how you ended up at the bottom of the sea and what has happened with the world above the sea. Sorry if i dont explain the story in that much detail but it's truely something that's best to be experienced yourself with no spoilers.
In terms of mechanics there is not a whole lot to talk about. The game controls pretty much exactly like Amnesia and Penumbra if you have played those games. Very simple click and drag and right click to throw what you are holding. CTRL for crouching and Space to Jump. Pressing "Q" to lean to the left and "E" to lean right. There is no real hiding mechanic as such. You cant hide underneath beds, or chairs or something like that to conceal yourself like you can in other horror games, like Outlast and Alien: Isolation. The only way to really hide is to just crouch behind furniture and hope that the monsters dont find you. That's really it for mechanics. The games pacing is very nicely done too. The game alternates between puzzle sections and story telling sections and horror sections very nicely to always keep you invested in the story. Though i will say that some of the puzzles in the game are tedious and just feels more like an annoyance more than a challenge.
Here is the most important thing. The sound and atmosphere in the game is truley something i haven't experienced in a game before. The sound design in this game is out of the park. It's excellent. From the sound of vague whale singing in the distance (Wich really scared me by the way) To the sound of your footsteps on the ocean floor. The game nails the feeling of being 10000 feet under the surface. And this is not to mention the enimies you will encounter in the game. Again i dont want to spoil too much but let's just say that they are horrorfying screams that will be stuck in your brain even after you stop playing O.O.
Now to the atmosphere. Like i have said the games sound really helps on the atmosphere. When you first step out onto the ocean floor and you look up and notice that you can barely see the sunlight, i truely strikes you that you are all alone down there with no one to help.
After walking around for a while i noticed something that looked like the edge of a cliff. I walked over to the edge and looked down and saw total darkness and seemingly no bottom. The ambient music kicks in and the vision of my character got very blurry as if he was about to pass out (Wich by the way i was about to in real life) Really freaky O_O
When you aren't outside in the big, vast, emptiness of the ocean, you are typically inside "Underwater-Facilities". Here is where you will encounter most of the enemies in the game. When you are inside these structures, there will be sounds of the building buckling under the immense presure of the water, and other audio cues that add to the atmosphere of the game and keep reminding you, that you are thousands of feet below the ocean. Wich is a horrorfying thought in and of itself.
Overall SOMA is one of the best horror games i have played to date. And it being underwater only made it scarier for me XD. If you are a horror fan i can recommend this. However if you are Thallasophobic you may have to reconsider since i had to stop playing the game for weeks on end sometimes because it was to much for me. But if you actually beat the game as a Thallasophobic the feeling of accomplishment makes it all worth it ;)

I am pretty sure I have never posted a review on here but felt compelled to do so for this game. I have loved this game ever since it came out 13 years ago and was really disappointed when even with all the online fixes, patches and workarounds I could find, I could not get it to work on my new pc or laptop.
I emailed the devs last year who said they were working on a version that would work with modern day computer's and their operating systems, but did not see anything further.
Then yesterday I see it drop on steam and immediately by it whilst it was on sale at £8 and I was upset to learn it still wouldn't work. Read some forums and tried a few workarounds including various different compatibility modes, but no dice.
I shut down my pc and rebooted and just as I was about to send an email to the devs, venting my frustration and requesting assistance or an eta on a fix, I decided to boot the game again (with no compatibility modes turned on), so that I could get the error code and Boom, worked first time and worked flawlessly all evening last night.
So to all who buy this game wanting it to work, try the workarounds, shut down and reboot your pc to try and make it work, you never know your luck. The fact it does work though on my PC which has an overlocked i7, GTX 780 ti, Windows 7 pro 64 bit, shows that there has been progress in making this game compatible with modern day PCS.
Unfortunately it does appear that its not universally working so yes its a risk, but if you played this game in the past and enjoyed it as much as I did, its worth the risk especially with the steam refund policy that now exists.

I honestly spent a good amount of time pondering whether to get this game. I've been wanting to get it on sale for a while now, but alas, no sale has popped up. Regardless I think you should buy this game, even for the full price of 40 bucks. Here's why:
Let me start off with my first 2 hours I played (where I tested the game to see if I wanted a refund).
In those 2 hours, I had gotten the chance to play multiple matches. Queue times for a game were always under a minute (which is impressive considering each game has an average length of maybe ~12 mins).
I played as Jason, and boy is it fun creatively murdering the survivors in often times unfair ways.
I died a few times as counselor as well, before hitching a ride in a car with some survivors and high tailing it outta there.
The gameplay experience is incredibly dynamic, and although I got into a few matches where no one had a mic, I also had others where everyone was communicating and having a blast.
When new, using the 3D VoIP to portray yourself as an actual counselor adds a lot of immersion and general fun. I distinctly remember being with a group of 3 other counselors when Jason came up and grabbed one of us. I swung my bat at him yelling "Leave my friend alone you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!" only to jump back in the car and get moving.
Everyone seems rather friendly, and the worst I've experienced when it comes to toxicity is the uncommon condescending, thinks he's better than you prick (I'll call them Chad).
There is a lot of progression available, from spending CP to roll perks, to buying new Jason kill animations. This of course is underneath a general ranking system that allows you to unlock survivors as you play more and more.
For those of you on the fence, I'd say buy this game, but only because I've been massively hyping it up in my mind. Regardless, this game is a lot of fun, even without friends, microphones, and with the occasional bull♥♥♥♥♥♥glitch (like when Jason gets shot in the eye with a flare gun and doesn't even flinch).
This game also differs from Dead by Daylight in mechanics and in purpose.
Dead by Daylight is very much a competitive game. While neither is scarier than the other, F13 proves to be more of an immersive experience (where you get the chance to be a part of the movie).

6ая часть легендарной серии Resident Evil.
Невозможно отрицать тот факт,что геймплей и атмосфера игры далеки от классических первых трех частей,что разумеется,не понравится любителям классики.Как и "новые" Resident Evil 4 и Resident Evil 5-эта игра шутер.Хоррор отсутствует,однако тем не менее в отличии от 5ой части,здесь делаются какие то намеки на него,в кампании Леона.
Кстати,насчет кампаний и сюжета.В игре 4 кампании,три из которых расчитаны на двоих игроков,где уже знакомые персонажи(Леон,Крис,Шерри) действуют на пару с новичками(Хелена,Пирс,Джейк),последняя же 4ая кампания играется за Аду Вонг.Несмотря на огромную продолжительность всех кампаний,как ни странно,они не надоедают(ИМХО).Сюжет не плох,ролики сделанны вполне себе хорошо,а геймплей не жданно не гаданно цепляет(ИМХО).Здесь вам и обычные перестрелки,и битвы с боссами и поездки на мотоцикле и прочем виде траспорта(включая вертолет),короче говоря,заскучать попросту невозможно(ИМХО),тем более,что патронов мало и часто приходится сражаться в рукопашную.
Думаете,пройдя кампанию можно смело забивать на игру?Только не в творении от Capcom,уж эти японцы умеют заставлять игроков засиживать за своими играми(пример-Devil May Cry 4).Помимо классического режима "Наемники",появившегося еще в 3ей части,имеется,впервые введенный в 5ой режим "Наемники:Возмездие" и еще около 3-5 новых режимов.А помимо "Дополнительного контента" здесь имеются всякие фигурки и документы про разные события и персонажей.
Теперь менее важные вещи:
Графика очень даже не плохая,радует глаз(ИМХО)
В саундтреке нет ничего примечательного,однако некоторые композиции можно выделить.
Получилось полноценное продолжение серии,сделанное на самом высшем уровне.(ИМХО)
Здесь они решили угодить всем,что стало их ошибкой,(кампания Криса полностью лишена атмосферы),однако игра в целом замечательная,не шедевр разумеется,но превосходный продукт,поглощение которого не надоедает очень долго,пожалуй никакая из игр серии Resident Evil доселе не имела настолько широких возможностей ни геймплея,ни дополнительного контента.Симбиоз всего лучшего из 4ой и 5ой частей.Если разработчики продолжат в том же духе и еще более приблизят последующую часть к классике,то Resident Evil 7 однозначно будет шедевром.

Seasons After Fall is not a bad game, but its not superb either, its just good. And because of the short gameplay, I recommend to wait for sale.

Full review:

**I received a code from the dev for this game**
WARNING: SPOILERS
First off, this is a GORGEOUSLY BREATHTAKING game. Myself and my viewers were constantly in awe of the stunning art style and graphics. The score was superb, and as a once upon a time band/orchestra geek, and avid lover of orchestral scores from video games, I have no complaints. The music set the ambiance extremely well, and maintained "the feels" throughout my entire playthrough.
The mechanics are remniscient of that of "Lost Winds" (Wii/PC-Steam) in regards to how the player manipulates the seasons in order to enact certain responses from the environment in order to solve the various puzzles in the game. I love puzzles, and quite enjoyed solving those concocted. The difficulty varied from easy to requiring much thought, all without holding my hand at any point. It was set up in a way that allows the player to gradually build upon their skills so that they don't feel overwhelmed, which is a great aspect for someone who doesn't usually play puzzle games.
As far as story goes, I thought it was a nice story, but also a bit hollow. Viewers kept asking what the game was about, and I honestly could not tell them aside from I play a possessed fox who controls the seasons to solve puzzles for some random talking voice that keeps calling me a "seed." The gist of the story wasn't obvious until the botched ritual scene, and even then it felt empty. I was hoping the various cutscenes as I released the guardians would provide more depth, but still found it lacking. WHY was the seed afraid? WHAT was she afraid of? After I beat the game and the fox remained dead, I just get, "we'll honor it," and that's it. I felt like there could have been more there.
The final thing for myself, is even though I don't care for cookie crumbs to hold my hand through the entire game, there were times I felt frustrated because what I needed to do wasn't entirely clear. I found myself doing a lot of backtracking in an attempt to trigger something, or find a location that wasn't necessarily apparent. There's no map, either, so if you are directionally challenged like myself, it can be woefully irritating at times. If not, this may not be something that bothers you. Regardless, it's not at all a deterrent nor a deal breaker.
Overall, I would recommend this game. Even with some of the things it's lacking, it's still a wonderful game, and very much worth the 8~ hours it took me to make it to the end credits. I look forward to seeing more content in various games from this developer.

I really expected to play an amazing game like Amnesia. The trailers are fantastic and the first hour is really immersive. Unfortunally the game fails to sustain itself.
In 2 hours or so you discover that the place you are in SEEMS big...but it's just a boring straight road with no turns whatsoever. Don't know for you, but I figured out how the WHOLE story would go after the first hour and a half (kept playng only to discover I was right).
The monsters chasing you are scary...the forst time...challenging AND scary for the second and third. But from the 4th encounter and on you just keep thinking
AGAIN?!" and all the baddies becomes more like a (stupid) idea to make the game longer forcing the player to stay hidden or risk his life and do everything from the start of the last chekpoint.
Also, the chekpoints are placed so well that is frustrating: practically a new checkpoint marks a new room, where you have to do THIS do get to the next one...that's all...that's the WHOLE game.
The story (not the game) is short and badly told since you can easily guess all the most important parts just after an hour or so in game, making the rest of the game almost futile...well the rest is supposed to point out the growth of the characters
The exploration in the game is almost pointless since there are no notes to read to understand better the story apart from some ill recorded messages that are placed ALWAYS in front of you in the main road. The world outside the main road you MUST follow is beautiful to see...but you see it once, maybe twice then it's always the same. Couple it with the useless (and sometimes risky) exploration and you have a nice shell for a game that could have been MUCH more but seems like the developers lost interest in it while they wrote the script.
I can suggest you to buy it IF it gets under 5 bucks...no more than that.

Thomas Was Alone is an indie 2D puzzle platformer created by
, released in July 2012. The game tells a story about friendship based on rectangular shaped character, using a narrator who leads the player through the game. The goal of the game is to lead each character to the end of a level in order to proceed to the next level. To complete a level, characters are required to work together and use their different abilities to help each other.
First of I have to say the game is really short, it took me about 1.5 hours to finish it 100%. This isn't necessarily a bad thing though, it depends on your personal preference. In my opinion the short playtime suits the minimalist style of the game. Another thing that might or might not be a downside is that the platforming as well as the puzzle aspect of the game is really easy, but like I said before, it's personal preference.
The music and the voice of the narrator complement each other very well, the audio overall creates a calm and appeasing atmosphere. The visuals are minimalist, which is a definite advantage in my opinion, and suit the basic gameplay and calm atmosphere of this game very well. The background and the environment is often in a dusky tone and the characters are light-coloured, which creates the lost feeling.
Thomas Was Alone combines great storytelling with an innovative visualisation, but I wouldn't recommend it to anyone who plays games as a pastime or anyone who plays just to win. This game isn't about winning or about beating it, it's about experiencing the story. It's about enjoying the art and watching the characters proceed. Thomas Was Alone is a great game, if you're the right person to play it.

Orwell is a GUI point and click choose your own text-based adventure.  Minimal audio limited to ambiance, punctuated occasionally by tension-inducing background music.  Intriguing story surrounding the security vs. privacy debate with real world implications.
Recommendation:  Get it during a sale; definitely worth playing!
PROS:
+ Relevant and topical story
+ Interface is easy to learn and feels natural
+ Plausible system mechanics aids in the suspension of disbelief
+ NPCs have interesting personalities
+ Difficulty increases at the end to maintain interest
+ Multiple endings with satisfying results; good replayability
CONS:
+ Minor text/grammar errors in a text-based game are bad, avoidable through QA/QC
+ Game is a bit short, can be beaten in just a few hours - which is why I recommend only getting it on sale
+ Listening in on phone calls looks/plays exactly like reading a text message conversation; i.e. boring
+ Can feel railroad-y, especially at the very beginning tutorial part

Simply put, Orwell condenses all of the moral arguments surrounding a surveilance state to a "let's see you do it."
You are responsible for guiding a PRISM-like system in a quest to unravel violent events surrounding a group opposed to the intrusions upon society.  Somewhat true to life, your superiors act on what information you condense down to them - they don't actually read everything (that's 'your job').  You get to eavesdrop, sift through a computer's hard drive, peruse the private accounts of citizens... all in a quest to 'do the right thing.'
The ethical dilemma is appropriate.  There is a very real threat to the game's citizens.  Yet, you can easily pass along information out of its proper context and paint a picture that doesn't exist from within the ocean-spray of people's activity on the internet.  Even very early into the game, you find yourself ignoring far more text than you are reading as the scope of the investigation expands and you find yourself 'scope locked' to the auto-tag system.
There is some replayability, as well.  Events are influenced by what information you pass along, as well as how you react to some real-time scenarios.
This is where it becomes interesting - your superior isn't entirely sure of everything you are seeing.  You can see that someone is planning a hack in real time... and just ... let it happen.  Or, you can see that a person suspects they are being monitored, and pass along tactical information that could be disinformation.  This is partially where the ethical context of the game comes into play, as the events can unfold in many different ways depending upon how you, as an individual, wish them to.  Don't like a person?  Try to land them in jail.  Like a character?  Try to shield them from the investigation ... or guide the investigation to them in order to justify unleashing the full resources of Orwell on their private life.
Perhaps the forest amid all the trees, however, is that the entire conflict of, at least, the first story arc would not exist were it not for the very system used to defend against it.
In all, it's a great exploration of the ethics of our evolving soviety.  Highly recommended for its philosophical exploration, alone.

Silence of the Sleep is a very uniquely designed horror adventure puzzle game. The biggest noticeable thing is that it’s a side scroller, but don’t let that fool you, that doesn’t take away from its horror elements. In fact it even improves its puzzle and adventure elements. The horror bit consists of the standard jump scares, but that’s just the cherry on top. The real fear is from personal anxiety and paranoia. The game isn’t all about horror though. There are some parts where there are no threats, and its pure exploration and talking to other characters. There are in total 5 chapters of gameplay, with chapter 3 focused on story and being relatively calm and 5 being the ending which is more handheld than anything. The game has a very similar feel to older horror games, specifically point and clicks. In General the game took me about 9 hours to beat, however some ran through it way faster or slower.
Pros
Unique design
Interesting color scheme
Interesting characters
Fulfilling ending
FANTASTIC music
Emotionally investing
Cons
Certain areas drag on a tad (house)
After a few deaths on a monster, that monster loses its scary element (it comes back with others)
Certain parts is just remember the monsters path (sewers)
Not necessarily a con but the game gives you multiple dialogue and action options, but they will only affect minor things, if at all.
I personally think the game is worth its price tag, however I did get it through the auctions, so my 2 cents might not be as valuable. If it is at least 15% off, it’s a must buy.

Silence of the Sleep is a strange little game.
It's advertised as a psychological horror game, and generally that fits, though it has its share of creepy visuals as well, mostly the horrible monsters that inhabit its surreal world.  Your mileage may vary on whether they are geniuinely scary, but the game creates a tense and unsettling atmosphere.  Do yourself a favor and devote real time to playing it in the dark without distractions.
The story is a bit wandery and you will be confused if you don't read absolutely every line of dialogue, but it isn't a major detractor--it gets its point across all the same.  You'll find yourself wondering where things are going to go next even after you've stopped playing.
The control scheme of the game is by far its weakest point, however, with a "semi-2D" plane which still requires some 3D navigation.  Turning is imprecise and sometimes lags, and this can make a frustrating difference when you're trying to dash into another room to escape a monster.  The game would have been far better off with click to move controls like most point-and-click adventure games--and at its core, that is what Silence of the Sleep is.  There is no combat, all you can do is run away and hide.  Most of the puzzles are fairly straightforward with a surprising lack of the usual "adventure game logic."  It's not a brain teaser but you will have to stop and think from time to time.
The game could also have used a proofreader.  There are some noticeable spelling and grammatical errors here and there.
In sum, if you won't be unduly bothered by its sometimes irritating controls and want to try something different, give Silence of the Sleep a try.  Let yourself be immersed in it, you won't regret it.

The strange thing is he does not actually die but plunges into darkness. He will find himself with most of his memories gone, and a very tricky path in front of him to leave the place that he finds himself in.
Graphically this definitely gives that creepy vibe of anything could jump out at you. You will go through several different locations, and they will range from fancy to dilapidated. This is almost a side-scroller but does have the 3D space feel to it as doors will be in front, behind, and to the side of you. The monsters that creep around this game and will kill you with quick ease are very nightmarish. I did find it interesting that everyone is cast in silhouette in this game, but it works.
The sound is going to be used as another layer of the game. There are certain sounds that when you hear them you know you are in trouble, and you either need to run or hide. I do wish that this game was voiced, it definitely would have furthered the immersion into the game.
The controls are really straightforward. You are going to use the WASD combo to move, 'e' to interact, and 'f' for flashlight (which you can use the mouse to gain a little bit more precision on where the beam is aimed. I will tell you this though, if you use 'w' or 's' to face back or forward, you will need to press 'a' or 'd' before you can face forward or back, with the exception of left and right, there is no 180 turns.
Alright so lets get into the meat of the game. You are going to be put on a path that is really a point A to point B type of situation. You are going to be put to the test through each section of the game, and each section has its own wrinkles. There are going to be puzzles that you will have to solve in order to advance the game, and sometimes the answers are not the most straightforward thing. You may miss something small, and that will haunt you as you are combing over each section of the game to try to get a combination, or a solution.
This game has a lot of back and forth to it through each section as you try to advance the game, there's also layers of gameplay that keep getting added, which I don't know if I really liked. The first real example of this is that you will get to a certain part of the game, after you have already run into at least one nightmarish monster, where all of a sudden you are now able to see through a peephole or listen to the door to try to determine where the monster is so that you can hopefully get past it and not get killed by it. This left me wondering why not start off the game with this ability. Then a little bit later you all of a sudden have an ability to hide from the monsters. Now I'm all for adding layers of complexity to the game, but this just feels like the developer decided to come up with ideas and throw them in as they went, never thinking about previous sections.
This is a tough game, and there's going to be those moments of absolute frustration, but as long as you save, A LOT, by interacting with the record players you find, you might find a hidden gem here. Personally this game doesn't feel as polished as I think it could have been, but there's definitely something to the game that kept me coming back. The story was interesting, I wasn't a HUGE fan of the font being used for dialogue, actually that was not a good choice, but the font didn't bother me to the point where I wanted to stop playing.
This is actually one tough game to rate. There are parts of the game that I didn't like and then there were pieces of the game that I liked. It is a good game, but at the same time there are things that just don't rub me the right way. So I guess I'm going to have to say that this game gets a 6.9 out of 10.

Silence of the Sleep is a strange little game.
It's advertised as a psychological horror game, and generally that fits, though it has its share of creepy visuals as well, mostly the horrible monsters that inhabit its surreal world.  Your mileage may vary on whether they are geniuinely scary, but the game creates a tense and unsettling atmosphere.  Do yourself a favor and devote real time to playing it in the dark without distractions.
The story is a bit wandery and you will be confused if you don't read absolutely every line of dialogue, but it isn't a major detractor--it gets its point across all the same.  You'll find yourself wondering where things are going to go next even after you've stopped playing.
The control scheme of the game is by far its weakest point, however, with a "semi-2D" plane which still requires some 3D navigation.  Turning is imprecise and sometimes lags, and this can make a frustrating difference when you're trying to dash into another room to escape a monster.  The game would have been far better off with click to move controls like most point-and-click adventure games--and at its core, that is what Silence of the Sleep is.  There is no combat, all you can do is run away and hide.  Most of the puzzles are fairly straightforward with a surprising lack of the usual "adventure game logic."  It's not a brain teaser but you will have to stop and think from time to time.
The game could also have used a proofreader.  There are some noticeable spelling and grammatical errors here and there.
In sum, if you won't be unduly bothered by its sometimes irritating controls and want to try something different, give Silence of the Sleep a try.  Let yourself be immersed in it, you won't regret it.

So our Boy Zero is a Solo Developer with a good idea. That Idea was to rip off every 4X game ever made, get people to buy a semi finished product and then buy the DLC which is basicly the fix for the broken game. Even at this (Abandoned) stage it is still pretty much a polished Beta.
So why am I recommending it?
Because it is fun to play. The AI is OK, the mechanics are all in place. Yes it gets a bit repeatative towards the end, but then most 4X games do.
StarDrive 1 had a thing where other Empires would just look at your empires power and surrender all control to you, which speeded up the final inevitable victory which this lacks. As was the whole game working in real time and being able to control your ships directly, which was a nice alternative to other 4X Turn based games, which was a fun, but I digress.
The tactical combat in this makes up for that (When it doesn't bug out), Think Imperium Galactica's space combat.
The Ground Combat is still a numbers game - Space bears Roll 20, Plant people roll 10+5 pointy stick techonolgy, like Master of Orion. But the Random Special Opperations and spy missions, Master of Magic style is a nice touch, if in need of some variation and expansion.
Interactions and treaties with the AI are handled nicely too. Weighting of technologies and explaintions of what you are doing that irks them.
The Graphics are basic but pretty, the UI is easy to get around and nothing that hasn't been seen before in every Sid Mayer game. If Buggy in places.
Yes the galaxy is paper thin but there are the occational thing to mix it up a bit, Pirate attack, Political unrest, Vengence/Life Goal/Just plain random missions from a Hero Character. If thease were expanded on this game would be truly amazing. Think along the lines of Endless Legend, but here the stories are never fully finished.
I look at other games like Polaris Sector, Stelaris and the New Master of Orion.
Slightly more expensive, the Tactical combat is treated OK by some and then badly by others. The glitchy AI on a complicated idea is forgivable is it isn't game breaking. But DLC to make the game playable, this is something of a♥♥♥♥♥♥take. So even some of the bigger studios are guilty of the same crimes as Zero.
So if you want to kill many hours leading your race of Space bears to colonise worlds afflicted with "Sharknados", ponder the best design of Space craft, before having T-Rexs with Guns stappled to thier heads break into a secret laboratory, this is the game for you.
That and you are resigned to the "Coming Soon" Features not coming at all.
I would love to see Zero properly finish a game and then release it, all the ideas fleshed out, it would probably be remarkable. As opposed to "Meh, brought it for the cost of half dozen beers, an it kept me occupied."

I loved the ambitions of SD1. Its main shortcoming was the ram limit issue, as most of its weaknesses were adressed by modders.
Hence, I had great hopes for SD2. I've played it for hours upon hours, and wanted to love it, however it feels lackluster in every aspect. Shortcuts have been taken to address the issues of SD1 (Hexmap to adress map complexity, Separating combat to a "combat phase" to avoid overloading the cpu and ram with massive battles...).
And even then, such shortcuts were not exploited to their full potential. Whereas most titles with "battle phases" allow for strategic troop placement, troop group controls (ctrl-1 2 3 etc), formations and such, SD2's battle phase is more similar to "totally accurate battle simulator" (google it), with the added bonus of selecting and moving individual or groups of units. That's it. You place your units and watch them fight. No quick groups, no formations, no path points, no tactics.
Diplomacy is equally lacking. AI's will continually attempt to rip you off, and show discontent when you refuse to comply to absurd demands.
If what you're looking for is a proper modern 4X, with a high degree of freedom, do yourself a favor and grab Stellaris.
And Zero, if you ever happen to read this : man, please, listen to your users. By trying too hard to "make something that works", you parted ways with all the aspects that made us love your first game. You used to be a dreamer, and this is why we used to love you. If you ever plan on releasing another game, by all means please either take your time or gather up with a proper team and come up with a masterpiece. More generic attempts like SD2 will never cut it when it comes to restoring the image you once had.

I bought the game and the DLC when they first came out. I also played the original Stardrive which, by the way, was abandoned by the developer because the technology behind that game was supposedly hindering the game's development. Alright, fair enough. I've been waiting for over a year now before giving my recommendation and here it is: don't buy this game.
Let me elaborate a bit.
I was eagerly anticipating Stardrive 2 when the developer first announced it. The game looked and felt fresh and seemed to be the game that will scratch that space 4X itch. The battles looked good with sufficient-enough depth and scope, there are interesting events happening throughout the galaxy, and the way the turns worked was also fresh. The user interface looked neat and the different AI races seemed interesting enough to warrant unlimited playthroughs.
Playing Stardrive 2 for the first time is like a dream. Designing your ships is fun, managing your colonies is fun, meeting the alien races is fun, going to battle is fun etc. I won't deny that for the first dozen hours or so, I've enjoyed my time with the game. Even the humor is well-placed.
Alas, after this honeymoon phase ends, you'll quickly get over the infatuation once you encounter all the bugs and the overall lack of polish, content and depth. Most noticeable is the game's lack of depth in terms of diplomacy and victory conditions. Sadly, after a while even the battles (which is the game's main strength) become boring and laggy.
It has most of the basic trappings of a 4x game... but many of these features feel tacked-on and underdeveloped. Take for instance the ability to customize your race  (ie. you can be sacrificers, slavers and others).  There are interesting choices there, but they are very limited. Another is the ability to customize your troops for special missions. This can be interesting and fun sometimes, however this part of the game is underdeveloped and limited. There are occasional special units and minor races, but these too are underdeveloped. By the 5th playthrough you've seen all the content the game has to offer.
The foundations for a great game are here. The IDEAs are there, sadly they weren't fleshed out. The game needed more time to develop and grow, but it was rushed out and, just like Stardrive 1, ultimately abandoned.
Avoid this game. In fact, avoid Zerosum games altogether.

It can be a little too easy sometimes, but it makes up for it in some other levels. You can wind up losing about 20 lives all in one level, expecially ones with poison minnows and mines. This game isn't widely popular, but it's a great game and deserves much more appreciation. Even if it's geared more towards kids, I think anyone can enjoy this game. I felt the need to write a review about this game just because I love it so much. I really hope to see more of these older games come to steam some day.

I put a good dozen hours into Feeding Frenzy on XBLA and enjoyed what it offered. Feeding Frenzy 2, in contrast, disappoints. The gameplay itself takes the first game and builds on it with bits like the various power ups, doing surface jumps for bugs, and so on. But playing this on PC isn't fun; movement is consigned entirely to the mouse with no controller support or mapping, and the game is locked in a 4:3 resolution.
This isn't surprising considering FF2D is an 11 year old title with no support from PopCap. Nor is it surprising that it is all but forgotten about except for the occasional burst of nostalgia of mid 00s pc gaming.
Gets points for working just fine from the get-go on Win 10 for me, but no controller or resolution alternatives means no recommendation of this game. Better to find a console version.
